events.title: Arnold Koller takes power
events.summary: Arnold Koller is a Swiss professor and politician. He served as a member of the Federal Council from 1987 to 1999 for the Christian Democratic People's Party (CVP). Koller previously served as a member of the National Council from 1971 to 1986. He did also serve two terms of the as President of the Swiss Confederation in 1990 and 1997.

events.title: Guillermo Endara takes power (imposed by a foreign power)
events.summary: Guillermo David Endara Galimany was a Panamanian politician who served as the president of Panama from 1989 to 1994.

events.title: 1990 Turkmen Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in the Turkmen SSR on 7 January 1990. Multi-party politics had been introduced but the Communist Party of Turkmenistan (CPT) remained the only registered party. With a voter turnout of 94%, the CPT won around 90% of the 175 seats.

events.title: Baku pogrom
events.summary: From January 12, 1990, a seven-day pogrom broke out against the Armenian civilian population in Baku, during which Armenians were beaten, murdered, and expelled from the city by Azerbaijanis. There were also many raids on apartments, robberies and arsons.

events.title: Battle: Black January
events.summary: Black January, also known as Black Saturday or the January Massacre, was a violent crackdown on anti-Soviet and anti-Armenian sentiments, Azerbaijani nationalism, and irredentism in Baku on 19 and 20 January 1990, as part of a state of emergency during the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Soviet Union vs APF (Azerbaijan)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Russia (Soviet Union) and APF over control of Azerbaijan, starting 1990-01-23. This episode was active in 1 year (1990–1990), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1990-01-27.

events.title: Rafael Leonardo Callejas Romero takes power
events.summary: Rafael Leonardo Callejas Romero was the 31st President of Honduras from 27 January 1990 to 27 January 1994, representing the National Party of Honduras (PNH).

events.title: 1990 Costa Rican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Costa Rica on 4 February 1990. Rafael Ángel Calderón Fournier of the Social Christian Unity Party (PUSC) won the presidential election, whilst his party also won the parliamentary election. Voter turnout was 81.8%.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Papua New Guinea vs BRA (Bougainville)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Papua New Guinea and BRA over control of Bougainville, starting 1990-02-07. This episode was active in 1 year (1990–1990), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1990-10-01.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Pakistan vs MQM
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Pakistan and MQM over control of the government, starting 1990-02-11. This episode was active in 1 year (1990–1990), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1990-02-11.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs Kashmir insurgents (Kashmir)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and Kashmir insurgents over control of Kashmir, starting 1990-02-12. This episode was active in 36 years (1990–2025), 5 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year) and was still active in the latest data.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Myanmar vs NMSP (Mon)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Myanmar (Burma) and NMSP over control of Mon, starting 1990-02-13. This episode was active in 1 year (1990–1990), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1990-03-22.

events.title: 1990 Uzbek Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in the Uzbek SSR on 18 February 1990. Of the 500 seats, 368 were decided in the first round. The result was a victory for the Communist Party of Uzbekistan, which won 348 of the 368 seats in the first round, whilst around 50 seats went to Unity.

events.title: 1990 Canadian federal budget
events.summary: The Canadian federal budget for fiscal year 1990–91 was presented to the House of Commons of Canada by finance minister Michael Wilson on 20 February 1990. It was the second budget after the 1988 Canadian federal election. Main estimates were tabled in the House of Commons on 22 February 1990.

events.title: 1990 Lithuanian Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in the Lithuanian SSR on 24 February with run-off elections on 4, 7, 8 and 10 March 1990 to elect the 141 members of the Supreme Soviet. In six constituencies, voter turnout was below the required minimum and a third round was held on 17 and 21 April.

events.title: 1990 Nicaraguan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Nicaragua on 25 February 1990 to elect the President and the members of the National Assembly. The result was a victory for the National Opposition Union (UNO), whose presidential candidate Violeta Chamorro surprisingly defeated incumbent president Daniel Ortega of the Sandinista National Liberation Front (FSLN).

events.title: 1990 Tajik Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in the Tajik SSR were held on 25 February 1990. A total of 230 deputies were elected to the Supreme Soviet.

events.title: 1990 Russian Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Legislative elections were held in the Russian SFSR in March 1990 as part of the regional elections across the Soviet Union. The first round was held on 4 March, and the second round on 14, 17 and 18 March. Members of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU) won 920 of the 1,068 seats, although several were supporters of the Democratic Russia movement.

events.title: 1990 Ukrainian Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in the Ukrainian SSR on 4 March 1990, with runoffs in some seats held between 10 and 18 March. The elections were held to elect deputies to the republic's parliament, the Verkhovna Rada. Simultaneously, elections of oblast councils also took place in their respective administrative divisions.

events.title: Hérard Abraham takes power
events.summary: Hérard Abraham was a Haitian military officer and politician who served as acting President of Haiti between 10 March 1990 and 13 March 1990.

events.title: Vytautas Landsbergis takes power
events.summary: Vytautas Landsbergis is a Lithuanian politician, musicologist and former Member of the European Parliament. He was the first Speaker of Reconstituent Seimas of Lithuania after its independence declaration from the Soviet Union.

events.title: 1990 Grenadian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Grenada on 13 March 1990. The result was a victory for the National Democratic Congress, which won seven of the 15 seats. Voter turnout was 68%.

events.title: Ertha Pascal-Trouillot takes power
events.summary: Ertha Pascal-Trouillot is a Haitian politician who served as the provisional President of Haiti for 11 months in 1990 and 1991. She was the first woman in Haitian history to hold that office and the first female president of African descent in the Americas.

events.title: 1990 Soviet Union presidential election
events.summary: The 1990 Soviet Union presidential election was held in the Soviet Union on 14 March 1990 to elect a president for a five-year term. This was the first and only presidential election to be held in the Soviet Union. This was due to the office of president being established in 1990, a year before the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991.

events.title: 1990 East German general election
events.summary: General elections were held in East Germany on 18 March 1990. These were the first free elections held in the region since the turbulent Weimar days of 1932 and would become the only truly democratic vote in the German Democratic Republic (GDR).

events.title: 1990 Latvian Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Latvian SSR on 18 March 1990. It was the first free parliamentary election in Latvia since 1931 and saw 201 deputies elected to the Supreme Soviet of the Latvian SSR, 170 of them in the first round. Run-off elections were held on 25 March 1 and 29 April. The Popular Front of Latvia won over two-thirds of the vote.

events.title: 1990 Estonian Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Elections to the Supreme Soviet were held in the Estonian SSR on 18 March 1990. Altogether 392 candidates ran for the Soviet-style legislature's 105 seats, of which four were pre-allocated to the military districts of the Soviet Army. The pro-independence Popular Front won the plurality.

events.title: 1990 Uzbek presidential election
events.summary: The first and last presidential elections in the history of the Uzbekistan Soviet Socialist Republic were held on March 24, 1990, one month after the elections to the Supreme Soviet of the Uzbekistan SSR.

events.title: 1990 Hungarian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Hungary on 25 March 1990, with a second round of voting taking place in all but five single member constituencies on 8 April. They were the first completely free and competitive elections to be held in the country since 1945, and only the second completely free elections with universal suffrage in the country's history.

events.title: 1990 Kazakh Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in Kazakhstan on 25 March 1990. Of the 360 seats, 270 were directly elected, whilst 90 were selected by public associations. The Communist Party of Kazakhstan won 342 of the 360 seats, with the remainder going to independents. Voter turnout was reported to be 84%.

events.title: April 1990 Bulgarian presidential election
events.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in Bulgaria on 3 April 1990 following the abolition of the State Council, the collective presidency of the Communist era. Members of the National Assembly elected a new president, with Petar Mladenov, former chair of the State Council, being elected unanimously.

events.title: 1990 Kirghiz Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in the Kirghiz SSR on 25 February 1990, with a second round on 7 April. At the time, the Communist Party of Kirghizia (PKK) was the only party in the country, with most of the candidates being from large collectives or state organisations.

events.title: 1990 Greek parliamentary election
events.summary: Early parliamentary elections were held in Greece on 8 April 1990. The conservative New Democracy party of Konstantinos Mitsotakis, was elected, defeating PASOK of Andreas Papandreou. In order to be able to command a majority of 151 in the 300-seat Parliament, New Democracy had to secure the support of Theodoros Katsikis, Democratic Renewal's sole MP.

events.title: Kyriakos Mitsotakis takes power
events.summary: Kyriakos Mitsotakis is a Greek politician, and the prime minister of Greece since July 2019, except for a month between May and June 2023. Mitsotakis has been president of the New Democracy party since 2016. He is generally associated with the centre-right, espousing economically liberal policies.

events.title: Soviet economic blockade of Lithuania
events.summary: The Soviet Union imposed an economic blockade on Lithuania between 18 April and 2 July 1990. By the late 1980s, Mikhail Gorbachev, leader of the Soviet Union, embarked on a course of liberalisation of the political system of the country, and as a result, movements appeared that advocated for autonomy or independence within the Soviet Union.

events.title: Golaniad
events.summary: The Golaniad was a protest in Romania in the University Square, Bucharest. It was initiated by students and professors at the University of Bucharest.

events.title: Milan Kučan takes power
events.summary: Milan Kučan is a Slovenian former politician who served as the first President of Slovenia from 1991 to 2002. Before being president of Slovenia, he was the 13th President of the Presidency of SR Slovenia from 1990 to 1991.

events.title: Violeta Chamorro takes power
events.summary: Violeta Barrios Torres de Chamorro was a Nicaraguan politician who served as the president of Nicaragua from 1990 to 1997. She was the country's first female president. Previously, she was a member of the Junta of National Reconstruction from 1979 to 1980.

events.title: European Council meeting (extraordinary)
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council (extraordinary meeting). Council presidency: Ireland.

events.title: József Antall takes power
events.summary: József Tihamér Antall, Jr. was a Hungarian teacher, librarian, historian, and statesman who served as the first democratically elected prime minister of Hungary, holding office from May 1990 until his death in December 1993. He was also the leader of the Hungarian Democratic Forum from 1989.

events.title: Ivars Godmanis takes power
events.summary: Ivars Godmanis is a Latvian politician who served as the Prime Minister of Latvia from 1990 to 1993 and again from 2007 to 2009. He was the first prime minister of Latvia after the country restored its independence from the Soviet Union.

events.title: 1990 Greek presidential election
events.summary: The 1990 Greek presidential election was an indirect election for the position of President of the Hellenic Republic was held by the Hellenic Parliament from February to May 1990.

events.title: Negotiations to end apartheid in South Africa
events.summary: The apartheid system in South Africa was ended through a series of bilateral and multi-party negotiations between 1990 and 1993.

events.title: Rafael Ángel Calderón Fournier takes power
events.summary: Rafael Ángel Calderón Fournier is a Costa Rican lawyer and politician who served as the 41st President of Costa Rica from 1990 to 1994.

events.title: Dinamo–Red Star riot
events.summary: The Dinamo Zagreb–Red Star Belgrade riot was a football riot which took place on 13 May 1990 at Maksimir Stadium in Zagreb, SR Croatia, then part of SFR Yugoslavia, between the Bad Blue Boys and the Delije.

events.title: 1990 Dominican Republic general election
events.summary: General elections were held in the Dominican Republic on 16 May 1990. Following a long vote count, Joaquín Balaguer of the Social Christian Reformist Party (PSRC) was declared winner of the presidential election, whilst in the Congressional elections the PSRC received the most votes and won a majority in the Senate, although the Dominican Liberation Party…

events.title: 1990 Romanian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Romania on 20 May 1990 to elect the President and members of Parliament. They were the first elections held after the overthrow of the communist regime six months earlier and the first free elections held in the country since 1937.

events.title: 1990 Romanian parliamentary election
events.summary: General elections were held in Romania on 20 May 1990 to elect the President and members of Parliament. They were the first elections held after the overthrow of the communist regime six months earlier and the first free elections held in the country since 1937.

events.title: 1990 Dominican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Dominica on 28 May 1990. The result was a victory for the Dominica Freedom Party, which won 11 of the 21 seats. Voter turnout was 66.6%, the lowest since universal suffrage was introduced in 1951.

events.title: Franjo Tuđman takes power
events.summary: Franjo Tuđman was a Croatian politician and historian who became the first president of Croatia, from 1990 until his death in 1999. He served following the country's independence from Yugoslavia. Tuđman also was the ninth and last president of the Presidency of SR Croatia from May to July 1990.

events.title: 1990 Osh clashes
events.summary: 1990 Osh riots were an ethnic conflict between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks that took place in June 1990 in the cities of Osh and Uzgen, part of the Kirghiz SSR. The immediate cause of the riots was a dispute between an Uzbek nationalist group Adolat and a Kyrgyz nationalist group Osh Aymaghi over the land of a former collective farm.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Indonesia vs GAM (Aceh)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Indonesia and GAM over control of Aceh, starting 1990-06-06. This episode was active in 2 years (1990–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-12-28.

events.title: 1990 Bulgarian Constitutional Assembly election
events.summary: Constitutional Assembly elections were held in Bulgaria on 10 June 1990, with a second round for eighteen seats on 17 June. They were the first elections held since the fall of Communism the previous winter, and the first free national elections since 1931.

events.title: Treaty signed: Dublin convention
events.summary: The Dublin Regulation was a regulation of the European Union that determined which EU member state was responsible for the examination of an application for asylum, submitted by persons seeking international protection under the Geneva Convention and the Qualification Directive, within the European Union.

events.title: John Turner resigns as Leader of the Liberal Party of Canada
events.summary: John Turner resigned as Leader of the Liberal Party of Canada on 23 June 1990, having held the office since 16 June 1984.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Ireland.

events.title: Cruzan v. Director, Missouri Department of Health
events.summary: Cruzan v. Director, Missouri Department of Health, 497 U.S. 261 (1990), is a landmark decision of the Supreme Court of the United States involving a young adult incompetent. The first "right to die" case ever heard by the Court, Cruzan was argued on December 6, 1989, and decided on June 25, 1990.

events.title: 1990 Serbian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Serbia on 1 and 2 July 1990, in which voters decided on approving a new constitution. The referendum was announced by Slobodan Milošević, the president of the presidency of SR Serbia, on 25 June.

events.title: 28th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union
events.summary: The 28th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union was held in Moscow. It was held a year ahead of the traditional schedule and turned out to be the last congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU) in the history of the party.

events.title: 1990 Moldavian Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Moldavian SSR in February and March 1990 to elect the 380 members of the Supreme Soviet. They were the first and only free elections to the Supreme Soviet of the MSSR.

events.title: 1990 Czechoslovak presidential election
events.summary: The 1990 Czechoslovak presidential election was held on 5 July 1990. Václav Havel was elected for his second term. Havel was the only candidate. Slovak National Party intended to nominate Štefan Kvietik who declined to run.

events.title: 1990 London NATO summit
events.summary: The 1990 London summit was the 11th NATO summit since 1949. The ones before had been in November 1985, March 1988 and May 1989.

events.title: Andrey Lukanov takes power
events.summary: Andrey Karlov Lukanov was a Bulgarian politician. Between February and November 1990, Lukanov was the final Prime Minister of the People's Republic of Bulgaria. He was murdered in 1996.

events.title: 16th G7 summit
events.summary: The 16th G7 Summit was held at Houston between July 9 and 11, 1990. The venue for the summit meetings was the campus of Rice University and other locations nearby in the Houston Museum District.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Iran vs KDPI (Kurdistan)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Iran and KDPI over control of Kurdistan, starting 1990-07-10. This episode was active in 1 year (1990–1990), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1990-08-17.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Israel vs Hezbollah (Southern Lebanon)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Israel and Hezbollah over control of Southern Lebanon, starting 1990-07-10. This episode was active in 11 years (1990–2000), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2000-11-26.

events.title: 1990 Armenian Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Armenian SSR on 20 May 1990, with further rounds held on 3 June and 15 July due to low turnouts invalidating earlier results. By 21 July, 64 seats were still unfilled, with 16 still unfilled in February the following year. The result was a victory for the Communist Party of Armenia, which won 136 of the 259 seats.

events.title: Leonid Kravchuk takes power
events.summary: Leonid Makarovych Kravchuk was a Ukrainian politician who served as the first president of Ukraine from 5 December 1991 to 19 July 1994. Kravchuk's presidency was marked by Ukraine achieving independence from the Soviet Union, the handover of its post-Soviet nuclear arsenal and an economic crisis that ultimately resulted in him losing re-election.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Mali vs MPA (Azawad)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Mali and MPA over control of Azawad, starting 1990-07-21. This episode was active in 2 years (1990–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-11-09.

events.title: Coup: Jamaat al Muslimeen coup attempt
events.summary: The Jamaat al Muslimeen coup attempt was an attempt to overthrow the government of Trinidad and Tobago, instigated on Friday, 27 July 1990.

events.title: 1990 Hungarian presidential election referendum
events.summary: A referendum on introducing direct elections for the Presidency was held in Hungary on 29 July 1990. Although the proposal was supported by 86% of voters, voter turnout was just 14%, resulting in the referendum being declared invalid. As a result, the President continued to be elected by the National Assembly.

events.title: July–August 1990 Bulgarian presidential election
events.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in Bulgaria in July and August 1990. A new president and vice president were elected by members of the Grand National Assembly following the resignation of president Petar Mladenov on 20 July 1990 less than four months after he was elected in April.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Iraq – Kuwait (Kuwait)
events.summary: UCDP records an interstate conflict between Government of Iraq and Government of Kuwait over control of Kuwait, starting 1990-08-02. This episode was active in 2 years (1990–1991), 2 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-03-01.

events.title: Iraq invades Kuwait
events.summary: The Iraqi invasion of Kuwait, codenamed Project 17, began on 2 August 1990 and marked the beginning of the Gulf War. After defeating the State of Kuwait on 4 August 1990, Iraq went on to militarily occupy the country for the next seven months.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Trinidad and Tobago vs Jamaat al-Muslimeen
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Trinidad and Tobago and Jamaat al-Muslimeen over control of the government, starting 1990-08-02. This episode was active in 1 year (1990–1990), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1990-08-02.

events.title: 1990 Hungarian presidential election
events.summary: The first indirect presidential election was held in Hungary on 3 August 1990, following the transition to multi-party democracy. Incumbent Speaker of the National Assembly and acting head of state Árpád Göncz was elected as president with more than three-quarter majority.

events.title: International sanctions against Iraq
events.summary: On 6 August 1990, four days after the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait, the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) placed a comprehensive embargo on Iraq. The sanctions stayed largely in force until 22 May 2003, and persisted in part, including reparations to Kuwait.

events.title: Log Revolution
events.summary: The Log Revolution was an insurrection which started on August 17, 1990, in areas of the Republic of Croatia which were populated significantly by ethnic Serbs. A full year of tension, including minor skirmishes and sabotage, passed before these events would escalate into the Croatian War of Independence.

events.title: 1990 São Toméan constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in São Tomé and Príncipe on 22 August 1990. The new constitution would introduce multi-party democracy for the first time since independence, as well as limiting the President to two terms. It was approved by 95% of voters. Parliamentary and presidential elections were held the following year.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Soviet Union vs Republic of Armenia (Nagorno-Karabakh)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Russia (Soviet Union) and Republic of Armenia over control of Nagorno-Karabakh, starting 1990-08-31. This episode was active in 2 years (1990–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-12-21.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Senegal vs MFDC (Casamance)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Senegal and MFDC over control of Casamance, starting 1990-08-31. This episode was active in 1 year (1990–1990), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1990-12-31.

events.title: Mircea Snegur takes power
events.summary: Mircea Snegur was a Moldovan agronomist and politician who served as the first President of Moldova from 1990 to 1997. Prior to that, he served as the Chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Moldavian SSR from 1989 to 1990 and chairman of the Supreme Soviet from 27 April to 3 September 1990.

events.title: Helsinki Summit (1990)
events.summary: The Helsinki Summit was a private, bilateral meeting between American President George H. W. Bush and Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev that took place in Helsinki, Finland on September 9, 1990.

events.title: Treaty signed: Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany
events.summary: The Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany , more commonly referred to as the Two Plus Four Agreement , is an international agreement that allowed the reunification of Germany in October 1990.

events.title: Revolution on Granite
events.summary: The Revolution on Granite was a student-led protest campaign that took place primarily in Kyiv and Western Ukraine in October 1990. Ukraine was then the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic, part of the Soviet Union until its declaration of independence on 24 August 1991. The protest was held from 2 October until 17 October 1990.

events.title: German reunification
events.summary: German reunification, also known as the expansion of the Federal Republic of Germany (BRD), was the process of re-establishing Germany as a single sovereign state, which began on 9 November 1989 and culminated on 3 October 1990 with the dissolution of the German Democratic Republic and the integration of its re-established constituent federated states into…

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Rwanda vs FPR
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Rwanda (backed by Government of DR Congo (Zaire)) and FPR over control of the government, starting 1990-10-03. This episode was active in 5 years (1990–1994), 2 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-07-04.

events.title: 1990 Austrian legislative election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Austria on 7 October 1990. The Social Democratic Party won the most seats, and retained the grand coalition with the Austrian People's Party. Voter turnout was 86%.

events.title: 1990 Temple Mount killings
events.summary: The 1990 Temple Mount killings, or the Al Aqsa Massacre, also known as Black Monday, took place in the Al-Aqsa compound on the Temple Mount, Jerusalem at 10:30 am on Monday, October 8, 1990, before Zuhr prayer during the third year of the First Intifada.

events.title: 1990 Azerbaijani Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in the Azerbaijan SSR on 30 September and 14 October 1990. They were the first multi-party elections in the country.

events.title: 1990 Liechtenstein tax referendum
events.summary: A referendum on modification of the legislation on national communal taxes was held in Liechtenstein on 21 October 1990. The proposal was rejected by 76.0% of voters.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Italy.

events.title: 1990 Turkmenistan presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held for the first time in the Turkmen SSR on 27 October 1990. The only candidate was Saparmurat Niyazov, who won 98% of the vote. Voter turnout was 97%.

events.title: Gro Harlem Brundtland takes power
events.summary: Gro Brundtland, known as Gro Harlem Brundtland, is a Norwegian stateswoman and former physician, who thrice served as the Prime Minister of Norway, and as the leader of the Labour Party from 1981 to 1992, and as the director-general of the World Health Organization from 1998 to 2003.

events.title: 1990 Irish presidential election
events.summary: The 1990 Irish presidential election was the tenth presidential election to be held in Ireland, the fifth to be contested by more than one candidate, and the first to have a female candidate and winner. It was held on Wednesday 7 November 1990, and was won by Mary Robinson on a joint Labour Party and Workers' Party ticket.

events.title: 1990–91 Guatemalan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Guatemala on 11 November 1990. with a second round of the presidential election held on 6 January 1991. The presidential election resulted in a victory for Jorge Serrano Elías of the Solidarity Action Movement, whilst the National Centre Union won the Congressional elections.

events.title: 1990 Georgian Supreme Soviet election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Georgian SSR on 28 October 1990, with a second round on 11 November. They were the first free parliamentary elections in Georgia since 1919 and saw Round Table-Free Georgia emerge as the largest party in Parliament with 155 of the 250 seats. Voter turnout was 70%.

events.title: Treaty signed: German–Polish Border Treaty
events.summary: The German–Polish Border Treaty of 1990 finally settled the issue of the Polish–German border, which in terms of international law had been pending since 1945.

events.title: Treaty signed: Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe
events.summary: The original Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe (CFE) was negotiated and concluded during the last years of the Cold War and established comprehensive limits on key categories of conventional military equipment in Europe and mandated the destruction of excess weaponry.

events.title: 1990 Polish presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Poland on 25 November 1990, with a second round on 9 December. They were the first direct presidential elections in the history of Poland, and the first free presidential elections since the May Coup of 1926. Before World War II, presidents were elected by the Sejm.

events.title: John Major takes power
events.summary: Sir John Major is a British statesman who served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Conservative Party from 1990 to 1997. He previously held various Cabinet positions under Margaret Thatcher. Major was the Member of Parliament (MP) for Huntingdon, formerly Huntingdonshire, from 1979 to 2001.

events.title: 1990 Conservative Party leadership election
events.summary: The 1990 Conservative Party leadership election was called on 14 November 1990 following the decision of Michael Heseltine, former defence and environment secretary, to challenge Margaret Thatcher, the incumbent Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, for leadership of the Conservative Party.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs ULFA (Assam)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and ULFA over control of Assam, starting 1990-11-30. This episode was active in 1 year (1990–1990), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1990-11-30.

events.title: 1990 Beninese constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Benin on 2 December 1990. The main issues were changing the political system to a multi-party system, with a secondary issue as to whether there should be age limits for the President. The referendum passed with 93% of voters approving the change to a multi-party system and 73% in favour of age limits.

events.title: 1990 German federal election
events.summary: A federal election was held in recently reunited Germany on 2 December 1990 to elect the members of the 12th Bundestag, within the regular time of nearly four years after the January 1987 West German federal election.

events.title: Coup: 1990 Chadian coup d'état
events.summary: The 1990 Chadian coup d'état took place on 1 December 1990 when the forces of the Patriotic Salvation Movement (MPS), a Libyan–backed rebel group under the leadership of General Idriss Déby, entered the Chadian capital N'Djamena unopposed. The MPS troops entered Chad by crossing the Sudanese border three weeks earlier.

events.title: Dimitar Iliev Popov takes power
events.summary: Dimitar Iliev Popov (Pokriva) (Bulgarian: Димитър Илиев Попов ; 26 June 1927 – 5 December 2015) was a leading Bulgarian judge and the first prime minister of the country not to be a member of the Bulgarian Communist Party since 1946. He was also the first prime minister since 1944 who was not a Communist or a fellow traveler.

events.title: 1990 Danish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Denmark on 12 December 1990. Although the election resulted in a strong gain for the Social Democratic Party, Poul Schlüter's coalition government was able to continue despite the Danish Social Liberal Party leaving. Schlüter's coalition consisted of the Conservative People's Party and Venstre.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Italy.

events.title: Treaty signed: Migrant Workers Convention
events.summary: The International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families is a United Nations multilateral treaty governing the protection of migrant workers and families. Signed on 18 December 1990, it entered into force on 1 July 2003 after the threshold of 20 ratifying States was reached in March 2003.

events.title: Alija Izetbegović takes power
events.summary: Alija Izetbegović was a Bosnian politician, Islamic philosopher and author who served as the president of the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1990 to 1996. He later served as the first chairman of the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1996 to 1998, and then briefly in 2000.

events.title: Lech Wałęsa takes power
events.summary: Lech Wałęsa is a Polish statesman, dissident and Nobel Peace Prize laureate who served as the president of Poland between 1990 and 1995. After winning the 1990 election, Wałęsa became the first democratically elected president of Poland since 1922 and the first-ever Polish president elected by popular vote.

events.title: 1990 Guinean constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Guinea on 23 December 1990. The new constitution was approved by 98.7% of voters, with a turnout of 97.4%.

events.title: 1990 Slovenian independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in the Republic of Slovenia on 23 December 1990. Both the ruling center-right coalition and the left-wing opposition supported the referendum and called on voters to support Slovenian independence.

events.title: Coup: 1990 Surinamese coup d'état
events.summary: The 1990 Surinamese coup d'état, usually referred to as the Telephone Coup, was a military coup in Suriname on 24 December 1990. The coup was carried out by the acting commander-in-chief of the Suriname National Army (SNL), Police Chief Ivan Graanoogst.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Myanmar vs ABSDF
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Myanmar (Burma) and ABSDF over control of the government, starting 1990-12-31. This episode was active in 3 years (1990–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-12-31.

events.title: Flavio Cotti takes power
events.summary: Flavio Cotti was a Swiss politician who served as member of the Federal Council from 1986 to 1999. He was a member of the Christian Democratic People's Party from the canton of Ticino. In the 1990s, Cotti led the Swiss government's unsuccessful attempts to further Switzerland's political integration into the European Union.

events.title: January Events
events.summary: The January Events were a series of violent confrontations between the civilian population of Lithuania, supporting independence, and the Soviet Armed Forces. The events took place between 11 and 13 January 1991, after the restoration of independence by Lithuania.

events.title: 1991 Portuguese presidential election
events.summary: A presidential election was held in Portugal on 13 January 1991.

events.title: Jorge Serrano Elías takes power
events.summary: Jorge Antonio Serrano Elías is a Guatemalan industrial engineer and politician who served as the 41st president of Guatemala from January 14, 1991 to June 1, 1993. He attempted a self-coup in May 1993 to stay longer in power.

events.title: Gulf War: coalition air campaign begins
events.summary: The Gulf War was an armed conflict between Iraq and a 42-country coalition led by the United States in response to Saddam Hussein invading neighboring Kuwait on 2 August 1990.

events.title: 1991 Crimean autonomy referendum
events.summary: A referendum on autonomy was held in the Crimean Oblast of the Ukrainian SSR on 20 January 1991, two months before the 1991 All-Union referendum. Voters were asked whether they wanted to re-establish the Crimean Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic, which had been abolished in 1945. The proposal was approved by 94% of voters.

events.title: 1991 Barbadian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Barbados on 22 January 1991 to elect all 28 members (MPs) of the House of Assembly of Barbados. The result was a victory for the ruling Democratic Labour Party (DLP), which won 18 of the 28 seats. The opposition Barbados Labour Party led by Henry Forde won ten seats, an increase of seven compared to the 1986 elections.

events.title: Nikola Kljusev takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: Nikola Kljusev was a Macedonian politician and professor of economics who served as the first Prime Minister of the Republic of Macedonia from March 20, 1991, to September 4, 1992, following the country's independence from Yugoslavia in 1991.

events.title: Battle of Khafji
events.summary: The Battle of Khafji was the first major ground engagement of the Gulf War. It took place in and around the Saudi Arabian city of Khafji, from 29 January to 1 February 1991.

events.title: Jean-Bertrand Aristide takes power
events.summary: Jean-Bertrand Aristide is a Haitian former Salesian priest and politician who served as president of Haiti in 1991, from 1994 to 1996, and from 2001 to 2004. He lived in exile between the 1991 military coup and 1994, and again between the 2004 coup and 2011.

events.title: 1991 Burundian Charter of National Unity referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the Charter of National Unity was held in Burundi on 9 February 1991. The charter would abolish ethnic discrimination and give a mandate for the government to write a new constitution. It was approved by 89.77% of voters with a 96% turnout.

events.title: 1991 Lithuanian independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in Lithuania on 9 February 1991, eleven months after independence from the Soviet Union had been declared on 11 March 1990. Just over 93% of those voting voted in favour of independence, while the number of eligible voters voting "yes" was 76.5%, far exceeding the threshold of 50%.

events.title: Coup: 1991 Thai coup d'état
events.summary: The 1991 Thai coup d'état was a military coup against the democratic Chatichai government, carried out by Thai military leaders on 23 February. Although the figure head was Sunthorn Kongsompong, there was a military influence from military leaders, Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, Suchinda Kraprayoon, and Kaset Rojananil in the conflict.

events.title: Treaty signed: Convention on Environmental Impact Assessment in a Transboundary Context
events.summary: The Convention on Environmental Impact Assessment in a Transboundary Context is a United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) convention signed in Espoo, Finland, in 1991 that entered into force in 1997.

events.title: Battle of 73 Easting
events.summary: The Battle of 73 Easting was fought on 26 February 1991, during the Gulf War, between Coalition armored forces and Iraqi armored forces. It was named for a UTM north–south coordinate line that was used as a phase line by Coalition forces to measure their progress through the desert. The battle was later described by Lt.

events.title: 1991 Latvian independence and democracy referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in the Latvian SSR on 3 March 1991, alongside a similar referendum in the Estonian SSR the same day. Known as the "Popular Survey about the independence of the Republic of Latvia", voters were asked "are you in favour of a democratic and independent Republic of Latvia".

events.title: 1991 Estonian independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in the Estonian SSR on 3 March 1991, alongside a similar referendum in the Latvian SSR the same day. It was approved by 78% of voters with an 83% turnout. Independence was restored by the Estonian Supreme Council on the night of 20 August.

events.title: 1991 protests in Belgrade
events.summary: Protests took place in 1991 on the streets of Belgrade, the capital of Serbia and Yugoslavia when a protest rally turned into a riot featuring vicious clashes between the protesters and police.

events.title: 1991 Salvadoran legislative election
events.summary: Legislative elections were held in El Salvador on 10 March 1991. The result was a victory for the Nationalist Republican Alliance, which won 39 of the 84 seats. Voter turnout was 44.7%.

events.title: 1991 Finnish parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Finland on 17 March 1991, the first time a Finnish parliamentary election had been held on a single day.

events.title: 1991 Abkhazian New Union Treaty referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the New Union Treaty was held in Abkhazia on 17 March 1991, as part of the wider Soviet referendum. The treaty was approved by 99.06% of voters.

events.title: 1991 Soviet Union referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the future of the Soviet Union was held on 17 March 1991 across the Soviet Union. It was the only national referendum in the history of the Soviet Union, although it was boycotted by authorities in six of the fifteen Soviet republics.

events.title: 1991 Ukrainian sovereignty referendum
events.summary: A sovereignty referendum was held in the Ukrainian SSR on 17 March 1991 as part of a USSR-wide referendum. Voters were asked two questions on reforming the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics into the Union of Sovereign States.

events.title: 1991 Russian presidential referendum
events.summary: A referendum on creating the post of President of Russia was held in the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic on 17 March 1991. The referendum was held alongside a referendum of the preservation of USSR.

events.title: Coup: 1991 Malian coup d'état
events.summary: The 26 March 1991 Malian coup d'état resulted in the overthrow of President Moussa Traoré after over two decades of dictatorship and eventually led to multi-party elections.

events.title: 1991 Georgian independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in the Republic of Georgia on 31 March 1991. It was approved by 99.5% of voters.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Sierra Leone vs RUF
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Sierra Leone (backed by Government of Guinea, Government of Nigeria) and RUF over control of the government, starting 1991-04-01. This episode was active in 11 years (1991–2001), 3 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 2001-12-20.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Iran vs MEK
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Iran and MEK over control of the government, starting 1991-04-03. This episode was active in 1 year (1991–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-04-03.

events.title: 1991 Belarusian strikes
events.summary: The 1991 Belarusian strikes, also referred to in Belarus as the April Strikes, were a series of nationwide strikes and rallies in the Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic.

events.title: European Council meeting (informal)
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council (informal meeting). Council presidency: Luxembourg.

events.title: Zviad Gamsakhurdia takes power
events.summary: Zviad Konstantines dze Gamsakhurdia was a Georgian politician, human rights activist, dissident, professor of English language studies and American literature at Tbilisi State University, and writer who became the first democratically elected President of Georgia in May 1991.

events.title: 1991 Albanian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Albania on 31 March 1991 to elect the 250 representatives of the People's Assembly. A second round was held on 7 April and a third round on 14 April. The elections represented a critical juncture in Albania's political evolution, transitioning from one party system to a multi-party liberal democratic system.

events.title: 1991 Icelandic parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Iceland on 20 April 1991. The Independence Party remained the largest party in the Lower House of the Althing, winning 17 of the 42 seats.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Iraq vs SCIRI
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Iraq and SCIRI over control of the government, starting 1991-04-24. This episode was active in 6 years (1991–1996), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1996-10-25.

events.title: Davíð Oddsson takes power
events.summary: Davíð Oddsson was an Icelandic politician, and the longest-serving prime minister of Iceland, in office from 1991 to 2004. From 2004 to 2005, he served as foreign minister and as the chairman for the Independence Party from 1991 to 2005.

events.title: Coup: 1991 Lesotho coup d'état
events.summary: The 1991 Lesotho coup d'état was a military coup that took place in Lesotho on 30 April 1991, led by Colonel Elias Phisoana Ramaema. It led to the resignation of Prime Minister General Justin Lekhanya, who held the office since the 1986 coup d'état.

events.title: Battle of Borovo Selo
events.summary: The Battle of Borovo Selo of 2 May 1991, known in Croatia as the Borovo Selo massacre and in Serbia as the Borovo Selo incident, was one of the first armed clashes in the conflict which became known as the Croatian War of Independence.

events.title: 1991 riot in Zadar
events.summary: The 1991 riot in Zadar was an act of violence that took place in the Croatian city of Zadar on 2 May 1991. Following an incident in the Zadar hinterland in which a Croatian policeman was killed, reportedly by SAO Krajina militiamen, Croatian civilians vandalized, destroyed and looted properties belonging to ethnic Serbs and Yugoslav companies in the city.

events.title: 1991 Yemeni constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Yemen on 15 and 16 May 1991. The new constitution was reportedly approved by 98.5% of voters, with a 72.2% turnout.

events.title: 1991 Cypriot legislative election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Cyprus on 19 May 1991. The result was a victory for the Democratic Rally, which won 20 of the 56 seats. Voter turnout was 93%.

events.title: 1991 Croatian independence referendum
events.summary: Croatia held an independence referendum on 19 May 1991, following the Croatian parliamentary elections of 1990 and the rise of ethnic tensions that led to the breakup of Yugoslavia. With 83 percent turnout, voters approved the referendum, with 93 percent in favor of independence.

events.title: Assassination of Rajiv Gandhi
events.summary: Former Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated by a suicide bombing in Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu on 21 May 1991. The incident resulted in the deaths of 17 people including Rajiv Gandhi and the perpetrator, 22-year-old Kalaivani Rajaratnam, a member of the Tamil militant organization Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).

events.title: 1991 Italian electoral law referendum
events.summary: An abrogative referendum on the electoral law was held in Italy on 9 June 1991. Voters were asked whether the clause of the law on the number of preference votes should be scrapped. The result was 95.6% in favour, with a turnout of 65.1%.

events.title: Mesut Yılmaz takes power
events.summary: Ahmet Mesut Yılmaz was a Turkish politician. He was the leader of the Motherland Party from 1991 to 2002, and served three times as Prime Minister of Turkey. His first two prime-ministerial terms lasted just months, while the third ran from June 1997 to January 1999.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Luxembourg.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Yugoslavia vs Republic of Slovenia (Slovenia)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Serbia (Yugoslavia) and Republic of Slovenia over control of Slovenia, starting 1991-06-28. This episode was active in 1 year (1991–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-07-03.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Spain vs ETA (Basque)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Spain and ETA over control of Basque, starting 1991-06-28. This episode was active in 1 year (1991–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-12-13.

events.title: Treaty signed: Brioni Agreement
events.summary: The Brioni Agreement, also known as the Brioni Declaration is a document signed by representatives of Slovenia, Croatia, and Yugoslavia under the political sponsorship of the European Community (EC) on the Brijuni Islands on 7 July 1991. The agreement sought to create an environment in which further negotiations on the future of Yugoslavia could take place.

events.title: First inauguration of Boris Yeltsin
events.summary: The first inauguration of Boris Yeltsin as president of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR) took place on Wednesday, 10 July 1991. The ceremony was held at the State Kremlin Palace and it lasted about thirty minutes. It was the first presidential inauguration ceremony in the history of Russia.

events.title: 1991 Mauritanian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Mauritania on 12 July 1991. The new constitution would restore multi-party democracy for the first time since the 1960s, as well as creating a bicameral Parliament with a Senate and National Assembly. The constitution would not include term limits for the President.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Turkey vs DHKP-C
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Turkey and DHKP-C over control of the government, starting 1991-07-13. This episode was active in 3 years (1991–1993), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-11-27.

events.title: 17th G7 summit
events.summary: The 17th G7 Summit was held in England between 15 and 17 July 1991. The venue for the summit meetings was Lancaster House in London.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs PWG
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and PWG over control of the government, starting 1991-07-16. This episode was active in 4 years (1991–1994), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-12-02.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Yugoslavia vs Croatian irregulars, Republic of Croatia (Croatia)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Serbia (Yugoslavia) and Croatian irregulars, Republic of Croatia over control of Croatia, starting 1991-07-27. This episode was active in 2 years (1991–1992), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-04-06.

events.title: Treaty signed: START I
events.summary: START I was a bilateral treaty between the United States and the Soviet Union on the reduction and the limitation of strategic offensive arms. The treaty was signed on 31 July 1991 and entered into force on 5 December 1994.

events.title: 1991 Mexican legislative election
events.summary: Legislative elections were held in Mexico on 18 August 1991, alongside gubernatorial elections in six states. The Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) won 320 of the 500 seats in the Chamber of Deputies and 31 of the 32 seats up for election in the Senate. Voter turnout was 61% in the Chamber election and 62% in the Senate election.

events.title: Coup: 1991 Soviet coup attempt
events.summary: In August 1991, hardliners of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU) attempted to forcibly seize control of the country from Mikhail Gorbachev, who was Soviet president and General Secretary of the CPSU at the time.

events.title: Boris Yeltsin takes power
events.summary: Boris Nikolayevich Yeltsin was a Soviet and Russian politician who served as President of Russia from 1991 to 1999, having previously served as Chairman of the Supreme Soviet of the Russian SFSR from 1990 to 1991. He was a member of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU) from 1961 to 1990.

events.title: Battle of Vukovar
events.summary: The Battle of Vukovar was an 87-day siege of Vukovar in eastern Croatia by the Yugoslav People's Army (JNA), supported by various paramilitary forces from Serbia, between August and November 1991. Before the Croatian War of Independence the Baroque town was a prosperous, mixed community of Croats, Serbs and other ethnic groups.

events.title: 1991 Sierra Leonean constitutional referendum
events.summary: A referendum on a new constitution was held in Sierra Leone in August 1991. Voting was held over four days. The new constitution would restore multi-party politics, as the country had been a one-party state since the 1978 constitutional referendum made the All People's Congress the only legally permitted party.

events.title: Edgar Savisaar takes power
events.summary: Edgar Savisaar was an Estonian politician, one of the founding members of Popular Front of Estonia and the Centre Party. He served as the acting Prime Minister of Estonia, Minister of the Interior, Minister of Economic Affairs and Communications, and twice mayor of Tallinn.

events.title: Ayaz Mütallibov takes power
events.summary: Ayaz Niyazi oghlu Mutallibov was an Azerbaijani politician who served as the first president of Azerbaijan. He was the last leader of Soviet Azerbaijan, and first President of Azerbaijan from 18 May 1990 until 6 March 1992 and from 14 May until 18 May 1992.

events.title: 1991 Macedonian independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in Macedonia on 8 September 1991, which resulted in the country proclaiming independence from Yugoslavia.

events.title: Battle of the Barracks
events.summary: The Battle of the Barracks was a series of engagements that occurred in mid-to-late 1991 between the Croatian National Guard and the Croatian police on one side and the Yugoslav People's Army (JNA) on the other.

events.title: 1991 Bangladeshi constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Bangladesh on 15 September 1991. Voters were asked "Should or not the President assent to the Constitution Bill, 1991 of the People's Republic of Bangladesh?" The amendments would lead to the reintroduction of parliamentary government, with the President becoming the constitutional head of state, but the Prime…

events.title: 1991 Swedish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Sweden on 15 September 1991. The Swedish Social Democratic Party remained the largest party in the Riksdag, winning 138 of the 349 seats. However, it was the party's worst showing since 1928 with 37.7% of the vote.

events.title: Stanislav Shushkevich takes power
events.summary: Stanislav Stanislavovich Shushkevich was a Belarusian politician and scientist who served as the first head of state of independent Belarus after it seceded from the Soviet Union, serving as the first chairman of the Supreme Soviet from 1991 to 1994.

events.title: 1991 Armenian independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in the Armenia SSR on 21 September 1991 to determine whether Armenia should secede from the Soviet Union. It followed a declaration of independence on 23 August 1990. 99.5% of voters voted in favour, with a turnout of 95%. The country officially became an independent state on 23 September 1991.

events.title: 1991 Liechtenstein referendum
events.summary: Two referendums were held in Liechtenstein on 22 September 1991. Voters were asked whether they approved of amendments to a law on noise protection, as well as introducing a five-day week at schools. Both proposals were rejected, by around 80% and 65% of the voters, respectively.

events.title: 1991 Kosovan independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in Kosovo, then known as the Socialist Autonomous Province of Kosovo between 26 and 30 September 1991.

events.title: Coup: 1991 Haitian coup d'état
events.summary: The 1991 Haitian coup d'état resulted in the overthrow of Jean-Bertrand Aristide, the democratically-elected president of Haiti, by a contingent of the Haitian military led by General Raoul Cédras and Chief of National Police Michel François.

events.title: Raoul Cédras takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: Joseph Raoul Cédras is a Haitian former military officer who was the de facto ruler of Haiti from 1991 to 1994. Cedras was the last military ruler of Haiti. He took power in the 1991 Haitian coup d'état against President Jean-Bertrand Aristide, and agreed to relinquish control of the government back to Aristide during Operation Uphold Democracy in 1994.

events.title: 1991 Kosovan independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in Kosovo, then known as the Socialist Autonomous Province of Kosovo between 26 and 30 September 1991.

events.title: Theodor Stolojan takes power
events.summary: Theodor Dumitru Stolojan is a Romanian politician who was Prime Minister of Romania from October 1991 to November 1992. An economist by training, he was also one of the presidents of the National Liberal Party (PNL) before being the founding leader of the Liberal Democratic Party (PLD) and then the Democratic Liberal Party (PDL).

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Haiti vs Military faction (forces of Raoul Cédras)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Haiti and Military faction (forces of Raoul Cédras)  over control of the government, starting 1991-10-02. This episode was active in 1 year (1991–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-10-02.

events.title: 1991 Portuguese legislative election
events.summary: The 1991 Portuguese legislative election took place on 6 October. The election renewed all 230 members of the Assembly of the Republic. There was a reduction of 20 seats compared with previous elections, due to the 1989 Constitutional revision.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ethiopia vs IGLF (Hararghe)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Ethiopia and IGLF over control of Hararghe, starting 1991-10-10. This episode was active in 1 year (1991–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-10-10.

events.title: 1991 Bulgarian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Bulgaria on 13 October 1991. They were the first elections held under the country's first post-communist constitution, which had been promulgated three months earlier. Voter turnout was 84%.

events.title: Levon Ter-Petrosyan takes power
events.summary: Levon Hakobi Ter-Petrosyan, also known by his initials LTP, is an Armenian politician and historian who served as the first president of Armenia from 1991 until his resignation in 1998.

events.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 1991
events.summary: The 1991 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting was the 12th Meeting of the Heads of Government of the Commonwealth of Nations. It was held in Harare, Zimbabwe, between 16 – 21 October 1991, and was hosted by Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe.

events.title: 1991 Swiss federal election
events.summary: Federal elections were held in Switzerland on 20 October 1991. The Free Democratic Party remained the largest party in the National Council, winning 44 of the 200 seats.

events.title: 1991 Turkish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Turkey on 20 October 1991, to elect members to the 19th Grand National Assembly. It was the first by the ruling Motherland Party to be contested without its founding leader, Turgut Özal, who had become Turkish president two years previously.

events.title: Treaty signed: 1991 Paris Peace Agreements
events.summary: The Paris Peace Agreements, officially the Comprehensive Cambodian Peace Agreements, was signed on 23 October 1991 and marked the official end of the Cambodian–Vietnamese War and the Third Indochina War.

events.title: 1991 Turkmen independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in the Turkmen SSR on 26 October 1991.

events.title: 1991 Polish parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Poland on 27 October 1991 to elect deputies to the First Term Sejm and the Senate, the two houses of the National Assembly. The 1991 election was notable on several counts.

events.title: 1991 Sandžak autonomy referendum
events.summary: The 1991 Sandžak autonomy referendum was held in Sandžak, Serbia, between 25 and 27 October 1991. Voters were asked whether they supported autonomy.

events.title: Madrid Conference of 1991
events.summary: The Madrid Conference of 1991 was a peace conference, held from 30 October to 1 November 1991 in Madrid, hosted by Spain and co-sponsored by the Soviet Union and the United States.

events.title: Carl Bildt takes power
events.summary: Nils Daniel Carl Bildt is a Swedish politician and diplomat who served as Prime Minister of Sweden from 1991 to 1994 and as leader of the Moderate Party (M) from 1986 to 1999. He served twice as Leader of the Opposition. He later held office as Foreign Minister under Fredrik Reinfeldt, serving from 2006 to 2014.

events.title: Kiichi Miyazawa takes power
events.summary: Kiichi Miyazawa was a Japanese politician who served as prime minister of Japan from 1991 to 1993.

events.title: Treaty signed: Alpine Convention
events.summary: The Alpine Convention (AC), formally the Convention on the Protection of the Alps, is an international treaty on the comprehensive protection and sustainable development of the Alps. The Convention is a pioneer of its kind as the first international treaty covering a whole mountain range that crosses several national borders.

events.title: 1991 Rome NATO summit
events.summary: The 1991 Rome summit was the 12th NATO summit bringing the leaders of member nations together at the same time. The formal sessions and informal meetings in Rome, Italy took place on 7–8 November 1991.

events.title: Filip Dimitrov takes power
events.summary: The 1990s in the People's Republic of Bulgaria and the Republic of Bulgaria.

events.title: 1991 Bosnian Serb referendum
events.summary: A referendum on remaining in Yugoslavia was held in the parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina with a significant Serb population on 10 November 1991.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Djibouti vs FRUD
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Djibouti and FRUD over control of the government, starting 1991-11-13. This episode was active in 4 years (1991–1994), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-03-04.

events.title: 1991 Equatorial Guinean constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Equatorial Guinea on 16 November 1991. The new constitution would replace the one-party state with multi-party politics. It was approved by 98.4% of voters with a 94.3% turnout.

events.title: Süleyman Demirel takes power
events.summary: Süleyman Sami Demirel was a Turkish politician, engineer, and statesman who served as the president of Turkey from 1993 to 2000. He previously served as the prime minister of Turkey seven times between 1965 and 1993. He was the leader of the Justice Party (AP) from 1964 to 1980 and the leader of the True Path Party (DYP) from 1987 to 1993.

events.title: 1991 Belgian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Belgium on 24 November 1991 to elect members of the Chamber of Representatives and Senate. The results represented a big loss for the majority parties and significant gains for the Vlaams Blok. The day became known as "black Sunday" due to the rise of the far-right party.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Burundi vs Palipehutu
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Burundi and Palipehutu over control of the government, starting 1991-11-27. This episode was active in 2 years (1991–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-04-14.

events.title: 1991 Ingush referendum
events.summary: A referendum on creating the Republic of Ingushetia within Russian Federation was held in Ingushetia on 30 November 1991.

events.title: 1991 Transnistrian independence referendum
events.summary: A referendum was held in Transnistria on 1 December 1991, in which Transnistria voted to continue its de facto independence and seek international recognition as a separate, sovereign country and member of the international community.

events.title: 1991 Ukrainian independence referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the Act of Declaration of Independence was held in Ukraine on 1 December 1991. An overwhelming majority of 92% of voters approved the declaration of independence made by the Verkhovna Rada on 24 August 1991. The public vote was held in response to the failed August coup and the New Union Treaty not being signed.

events.title: 1991 Transcarpathian general regional referendum
events.summary: The 1991 Transcarpathian general regional referendum took place on December 1, 1991, on the same day as the Ukrainian independence referendum and the first presidential elections in Ukraine. The question of the referendum was "On the granting Transcarpathian region status of an autonomous province within Ukraine."

events.title: 1991 Moldovan presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Moldova on 8 December 1991. Due to a boycott by the Popular Front of Moldova, incumbent Mircea Snegur was the only candidate to contest the elections and was elected unopposed.

events.title: 1991 Romanian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Romania on 8 December 1991. The new constitution was approved by 79% of voters.

events.title: Treaty signed: Belovezha Accords
events.summary: The Agreement on the creation of the Commonwealth of Independent States (officially), or unofficially the Minsk Agreement and best known as the Belovezha Accords, is the agreement declaring that the Soviet Union (USSR) had effectively ceased to exist and establishing the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) in its place as an organization created by the…

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Algeria vs Takfir wa'l Hijra
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Algeria and Takfir wa'l Hijra over control of the government, starting 1991-12-09. This episode was active in 28 years (1991–2018), 6 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 2018-11-19.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Netherlands.

events.title: 1991 Nagorno-Karabakh independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in Nagorno-Karabakh on 10 December 1991. It was approved by 99.98% of voters.

events.title: Grande Arche Congress
events.summary: The Grande Arche Congress was the fourteenth national congress of the French Socialist Party. It took place from 13 to 15 December 1991. The Congress marked a return to calm after the chaotic Rennes Congress.

events.title: Patrick Manning takes power
events.summary: Patrick Augustus Mervyn Manning was a Trinidadian politician who served as the fourth prime minister of Trinidad and Tobago twice from 1991 to 1995, and again from 2001 to 2010.

events.title: 1991 Trinidad and Tobago general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Trinidad and Tobago on 16 December 1991. The result was a victory for the People's National Movement, which won 21 of the 36 seats. Voter turnout was 65.5%.

events.title: Coup: 1991–1992 Georgian coup d'état
events.summary: The 1991–1992 Georgian coup d'état, also known as the Tbilisi War, or the Putsch of 1991–1992, was an internal military conflict that took place in the newly independent Republic of Georgia following the fall of the Soviet Union, from 22 December 1991 to 6 January 1992.

events.title: Lojze Peterle takes power
events.summary: Alojz "Lojze" Peterle is a Slovenian politician. He is a member of New Slovenia, part of the European People's Party. He served as Prime Minister of Slovenia from 1990 to 1992, Leader of the Christian Democrats from the founding of the party in 1990 until it merged with the Slovenian People's Party in 2000, and was Minister of Foreign Affairs from 1993 to…

events.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
events.summary: On 26 December 1991, the Soviet Union was formally dissolved and ceased to exist as a sovereign state and subject of international law.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Georgia vs National Guard and Mkhedrioni
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Georgia and National Guard and Mkhedrioni over control of the government, starting 1991-12-28. This episode was active in 3 years (1991–1993), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-11-16.

events.title: 1991 Azerbaijani independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in Azerbaijan on 29 December 1991, three days after the collapse of the Soviet Union. The result was 99.8% in favour of a constitutional act on the independence of the Republic of Azerbaijan, with turnout reported to be 95%.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Myanmar vs RSO (Arakan)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Myanmar (Burma) and RSO over control of Arakan, starting 1991-12-29. This episode was active in 1 year (1991–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-12-29.

events.title: 1991 Uzbek independence election
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in the Republic of Uzbekistan on 29 December 1991, alongside presidential elections and three days after the breakup of the USSR that Uzbekistan had previously declared independence from. The result was 98% of voters in favour, with a turnout of 94%.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Azerbaijan vs Republic of Artsakh (Artsakh (Nagorno-Karabakh))
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Azerbaijan and Republic of Artsakh (backed by Government of Armenia) over control of Artsakh (Nagorno-Karabakh), starting 1991-12-30. This episode was active in 4 years (1991–1994), 3 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-07-15.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Angola vs FLEC-R (Cabinda)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Angola and FLEC-R over control of Cabinda, starting 1991-12-31. This episode was active in 2 years (1991–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-12-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Myanmar vs NSCN-K (Nagaland)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Myanmar (Burma) and NSCN-K over control of Nagaland, starting 1991-12-31. This episode was active in 1 year (1991–1991), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1991-12-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Niger vs FLAA
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Niger and FLAA over control of the government, starting 1991-12-31. This episode was active in 2 years (1991–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-12-18.

events.title: René Felber takes power
events.summary: René Felber was a Swiss politician. He was a member of the Swiss Federal Council from 1987 to 1993. In 1992, he served as the president of Switzerland.

events.title: Jaba Ioseliani takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: Jaba Ioseliani was a Georgian politician, member of Parliament of Georgia, writer, thief-in-law and leader of the paramilitary organisation Mkhedrioni.

events.title: Terrorist attack: Algerian Civil War
events.summary: The Algerian Civil War, known in Algeria as the Black Decade, was a civil war fought between the Algerian government and various Islamist rebel groups from 11 January 1992 to 8 February 2002.

events.title: 1992 Bulgarian presidential election
events.summary: Direct presidential elections were held for the first time in Bulgaria on 12 January 1992, with a second round on 19 January. The result was a victory for incumbent President Zhelyu Zhelev of the Union of Democratic Forces, who won 52.8% of the vote in the second round. Voter turnout was 75.4% in the first round and 75.9% in the second.

events.title: 1992 Malian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Mali on 12 January 1992. The new constitution would restore multi-party democracy, create a division of powers between the President and National Assembly, and set a presidential term of five limits. It was approved by 99% of voters with a 44% turnout.

events.title: 1992 Macedonian Albanian autonomy referendum
events.summary: Ilirida or the Republic of Ilirida is a proposed state in the western regions of North Macedonia, declared twice by the politician Nevzat Halili, once in 1992 and again in 2014. The proposal has been declared unconstitutional by the Macedonian government.

events.title: 1992 South Ossetian independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in South Ossetia on 19 January 1992. The voters answered the questions: "Do you agree that South Ossetia should be an independent country?" and "Do you agree with the South Ossetian parliament solution of September 1, 1991 on reunion with Russia?" The proposals were approved by 99.9% of voters, but the results were not…

events.title: Tiit Vähi takes power
events.summary: Tiit Vähi is an Estonian politician who was Prime Minister of Estonia from 1995 to 1997. He was also acting Prime Minister for several months during 1992 under the transitional government.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Venezuela vs Military faction (forces of Hugo Chávez)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Venezuela and Military faction (forces of Hugo Chávez)  over control of the government, starting 1992-02-04. This episode was active in 1 year (1992–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-11-27.

events.title: Treaty signed: Treaty on European Union
events.summary: The Treaty on European Union (2007) is one of the primary Treaties of the European Union, alongside the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). The TEU forms the basis of EU law, by setting out general principles of the EU's purpose, the governance of its central institutions, as well as the rules on external, foreign and security policy.

events.title: Treaty signed: Maastricht Treaty
events.summary: The Treaty on European Union, commonly known as the Maastricht Treaty, is the foundation treaty of the European Union (EU).

events.title: Albert Reynolds takes power
events.summary: Albert Martin Reynolds was an Irish Fianna Fáil politician who served as Taoiseach and Leader of Fianna Fáil from 1992 to 1994. Between 1979 and 1991, he held several cabinet positions, including Minister for Finance from 1988 to 1991. He served as a Teachta Dála (TD) for Longford–Roscommon from 1977 to 1992, and for Longford–Westmeath from 1992 to 2002.

events.title: Assassination of Abbas al-Musawi
events.summary: On 16 February 1992, Abbas al-Musawi, the secretary-general of Hezbollah, was assassinated in an Israeli airstrike on his vehicle in southern Lebanon, as part of the South Lebanon conflict (1985–2000). Israel code-named the operation Night Time Operation.

events.title: 1992 Maltese general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Malta on 22 February 1992. The Nationalist Party remained the largest party, winning 34 of the 65 seats.

events.title: 1992 Montenegrin sovereignty referendum
events.summary: The 1992 Montenegrin sovereignty referendum was the first referendum regarding Montenegrin sovereignty, held on 1 March 1992 in SR Montenegro, a constituent republic of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

events.title: 1992 Bosnian independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina between 29 February and 1 March 1992, following the first free elections of 1990 and the rise of ethnic tensions that eventually led to the breakup of Yugoslavia.

events.title: Ayaz Mutallibov resigns as President of Azerbaijan
events.summary: Ayaz Mutallibov resigned as President of Azerbaijan on 6 March 1992, having held the office since 5 February 1991.
