events.title: Jean-Luc Dehaene takes power
events.summary: Jean Luc Joseph Marie "Jean-Luc" Dehaene was a Belgian politician who served as the prime minister of Belgium from 1992 until 1999. During his political career, he was nicknamed "The Plumber", as well as "The Minesweeper", for his ability to negotiate political deadlocks.

events.title: Eduard Shevardnadze takes power
events.summary: Eduard Ambrosis dze Shevardnadze was a Soviet and Georgian politician and diplomat who governed Georgia for several non-consecutive periods from 1972 until his resignation in 2003 and also served as the final Soviet minister of foreign affairs from 1985 to 1991.

events.title: Terrorist attack: 1992 Buenos Aires Israeli embassy bombing
events.summary: The attack on the Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires was a suicide bombing attack on the building of the Israeli embassy of Argentina, located in Buenos Aires, which was carried out on 17 March 1992. 29 civilians were killed in the attack and 242 additional civilians were injured.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Moldova vs PMR (Dniestr)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Moldova and PMR over control of Dniestr, starting 1992-03-17. This episode was active in 1 year (1992–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-07-31.

events.title: 1992 South African apartheid referendum
events.summary: A referendum on ending apartheid was held in South Africa on 17 March 1992. The referendum was limited to white South African voters, who were asked whether or not they supported the negotiated reforms begun by State President F. W. de Klerk two years earlier, in which he proposed to end the apartheid system that had been implemented since 1948.

events.title: 1992 Tatarstani sovereignty referendum
events.summary: A sovereignty referendum was held in Tatarstan, Russia, on 21 March 1992. Voters were asked whether they approved of Tatarstan being a sovereign state.

events.title: Treaty signed: Treaty on Open Skies
events.summary: The Treaty on Open Skies establishes a program of unarmed aerial surveillance flights over the entire territory of its participants. The treaty is designed to enhance mutual understanding and confidence by giving all participants, regardless of size, a direct role in gathering information about military forces and activities of concern to them.

events.title: 1992 Albanian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Albania on 22 March 1992, with a second round of voting for eleven seats on 29 March. The result was a victory for the opposition Democratic Party of Albania, which won 92 of the 140 seats. After the elections Aleksandër Meksi became prime minister and Sali Berisha became president.

events.title: P. J. Patterson takes power
events.summary: Percival Noel James Patterson,, popularly known as P. J. Patterson, is a Jamaican former politician who served as the sixth prime minister of Jamaica from 1992 to 2006. He served in office for 14 years, making him the longest-serving prime minister in Jamaica's history. He was the leader of the People's National Party from 1992 to 2006.

events.title: 1992 Andorran parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Andorra on 5 April 1992, with a second round of voting on 12 April. Following the elections, Òscar Ribas Reig remained Prime Minister.

events.title: 1992 anti-war protests in Sarajevo
events.summary: On 5 April 1992, in response to events all over Bosnia and Herzegovina 100,000 people of all nationalities turned out for a peace rally in Sarajevo. Serb Democratic Party (SDS) snipers in the Holiday Inn in the heart of Sarajevo opened fire on the crowd, killing six people and wounding several more.

events.title: 1992 Italian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Italy on 5 and 6 April 1992. They were the first without the traditionally second most important political force in Italian politics, the Italian Communist Party (PCI), which had been disbanded in 1991.

events.title: Coup: 1992 Peruvian self-coup
events.summary: The 1992 Peruvian self-coup, sometimes known as the Fujimorazo, was performed in Peru in 1992 after President Alberto Fujimori dissolved the Congress as well as the judiciary and assumed full legislative and judicial powers.

events.title: Sali Berisha takes power
events.summary: Sali Berisha is an Albanian politician and retired cardiologist who served as the President of Albania from 1992 to 1997 and as the 32nd prime minister of Albania from 2005 to 2013. Berisha has served as chairman of the Democratic Party of Albania since 2022. He has previously held the position of chairman from 1990 to 1992 and 1997 to 2013.

events.title: 1992 United Kingdom general election
events.summary: A general election was held in the United Kingdom on Thursday 9 April 1992, to elect 651 members to the House of Commons. The governing Conservative Party led by Prime Minister John Major won a fourth consecutive election victory, with a majority of 21.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Bosnia-Herzegovina vs Serbian irregulars, Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina (Serb)
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Serbian irregulars, Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina (backed by Government of Serbia (Yugoslavia)) over control of Serb, starting 1992-04-27. This episode was active in 4 years (1992–1995), 4 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1995-12-14.

events.title: 1992 Saint Lucian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Saint Lucia on 27 April 1992. The result was a victory for the United Workers Party, which won eleven of the seventeen seats. Voter turnout was 62.8%.

events.title: 1992 Ghanaian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A referendum on a new constitution was held in Ghana on 28 April 1992. The new constitution provided for the reintroduction of multi-party politics and the division of powers between the president and parliament.

events.title: Coup: 1992 Sierra Leonean coup d'état
events.summary: The 1992 Sierra Leonean coup d'état was a coup d'état against the government of Sierra Leone by a group of young military officers led by 25-year-old Captain Valentine Strasser on 29 April 1992. Strasser took control of the government, deposing President Joseph Saidu Momoh.

events.title: 1992 Los Angeles riots
events.summary: Los Angeles, California, experienced a series of riots and civil disturbances from April 29 to May 3, 1992. Civil unrest began in South Central Los Angeles on April 29, after a jury acquitted four officers of the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) charged with using excessive force in the arrest and beating of Rodney King.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Croatia vs Serbian irregulars, Serbian Republic of Krajina (Serb)
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Croatia and Serbian irregulars, Serbian Republic of Krajina (backed by Government of Serbia (Yugoslavia)) over control of Serb, starting 1992-04-30. This episode was active in 4 years (1992–1995), 2 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1995-09-13.

events.title: Battle: 1992 Yugoslav People's Army column incident in Sarajevo
events.summary: The 1992 Yugoslav People's Army column incident in Sarajevo occurred on 3 May 1992 in Dobrovoljačka Street, Sarajevo, when members of the Bosnian Army (ARBiH) attacked a convoy of the Yugoslav Army (JNA) troops that were exiting the city of Sarajevo according to the withdrawal agreement.

events.title: Treaty signed: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
events.summary: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) is the UN process for negotiating an agreement to limit dangerous climate change. It is an international treaty among countries to combat "dangerous human interference with the climate system". The main way to do this is limiting the increase in greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Tajikistan vs PFT, UTO
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Tajikistan (backed by  Government of Uzbekistan) and PFT, UTO (backed by  Government of Uzbekistan) over control of the government, starting 1992-05-10. This episode was active in 7 years (1992–1998), 3 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1998-11-16.

events.title: Ayaz Mütallibov takes power
events.summary: Ayaz Niyazi oghlu Mutallibov was an Azerbaijani politician who served as the first president of Azerbaijan. He was the last leader of Soviet Azerbaijan, and first President of Azerbaijan from 18 May 1990 until 6 March 1992 and from 14 May until 18 May 1992.

events.title: Janez Drnovšek takes power
events.summary: Janez Drnovšek was a Slovenian liberal politician, President of the Presidency of Yugoslavia (1989–1990), Prime Minister of Slovenia and President of Slovenia (2002–2007).

events.title: Coup: Black May (Thailand)
events.summary: Black May, also known as "Bloody May", was a series of mass protests and subsequent crackdowns by the Thai military and royal police in Bangkok in May 1992. A rally of over 200,000 people led by Chamlong Srimuang was held on 17 May, caused by the extending of the military regime of Suchinda Kraprayoon, the 1991 Thai coup d'état leader.

events.title: Gambarov takes power (irregular seizure of power)
Terrorist attack: Capaci bombing
events.summary: The Capaci bombing was a terror attack by the Sicilian Mafia that took place on 23 May 1992 on the A29 motorway, close to the junction of Capaci, Sicily.

events.title: 1992 Lithuanian presidency referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the presidency was held in Lithuania on 23 May 1992. Voters were asked whether they approved of restoring the institution of the presidency. It was initiated by Sąjūdis.

events.title: Treaty signed: Lisbon Protocol
events.summary: The Lisbon Protocol to the 1991 Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty was a document signed by representatives of Belarus, Kazakhstan, Russia, and Ukraine that recognized the four states as successors of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics and all of them assume obligations of the Soviet Union under the START I treaty.

events.title: 1992 Austrian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Austria on 26 April 1992, with a second round held on 24 May 1992 after no candidate won a majority in the first round. Incumbent president Kurt Waldheim did not seek reelection as he had not gained acceptance in the international community.

events.title: 1992 Italian presidential election
events.summary: The 1992 Italian presidential election was held in Italy on 13–25 May 1992, following the resignation of President Francesco Cossiga on 28 April 1992.

events.title: 1992 Danish Maastricht Treaty referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the Maastricht Treaty for the founding of the European Union was held in Denmark on 2 June 1992. The treaty was rejected by 50.7% of voters with a turnout of 83.1%. This meant a serious hurdle on the way in the process of further European integration, which nevertheless did continue because all twelve member states did want to ratify.

events.title: 1992 Azerbaijani presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Azerbaijan on 7 June 1992. The elections were the first in Azerbaijan in more than seventy years not held under communist control and featured the unprecedented use of television, posters, and other media by multiple candidates to communicate platforms and solicit votes.

events.title: 1992 Comorian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in the Comoros on 7 June 1992. The proposed amendments to the constitution were approved by 76% of voters, with voter turnout at around 64%.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Georgia vs Republic of South Ossetia (South Ossetia)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Georgia and Republic of South Ossetia over control of South Ossetia, starting 1992-06-08. This episode was active in 1 year (1992–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-08-14.

events.title: Treaty signed: Convention on Biological Diversity
events.summary: The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), known informally as the Biodiversity Convention, is a multilateral treaty. The Convention has three main goals: the conservation of biological diversity ; the sustainable use of its components; and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.

events.title: 1992 Lithuanian Soviet withdrawal referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the withdrawal of Soviet troops was held in Lithuania on 14 June 1992. Voters were asked whether Soviet troops should unconditionally and immediately withdraw from the country. It was approved by 93% of those voting and 69% of all registered voters, passing the 50% threshold.

events.title: Abülfaz Elçibay takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: Abulfaz Gadirgulu oghlu Aliyev, commonly known as Abulfaz Elchibey, was a Azerbaijani nationalist and Soviet dissident who was the first, and as of today, only democratically elected president of post-Soviet Azerbaijan.

events.title: Eleventh Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
events.summary: The Eleventh Amendment of the Constitution Act 1992 is an amendment to the Constitution of Ireland which permitted the state to ratify the Treaty on European Union, commonly known as the Maastricht Treaty. It was approved by referendum on 18 June 1992 and signed into law on 16 July of the same year.

events.title: 1992 Israeli legislative election
events.summary: Elections for the 13th Knesset were held in Israel on 23 June 1992. The election resulted in the formation of a Labor government, led by Yitzhak Rabin, helped by the failure of several small right wing parties to pass the electoral threshold. Voter turnout was 77%.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Portugal.

events.title: 1992 Estonian referendum
events.summary: A referendum on a new constitution and citizenship was held in Estonia on 28 June 1992. Voters were asked whether they approved of the new constitution drawn up by the Constitutional Assembly and extending suffrage to people who had applied for citizenship by 5 June.

events.title: Giuliano Amato takes power
events.summary: Giuliano Amato is an Italian politician who twice served as Prime Minister of Italy, first from 1992 to 1993 and again from 2000 to 2001. Upon Arnaldo Forlani's death in July 2023, Amato became the country's earliest-serving surviving Prime Minister.

events.title: Assassination of Mohamed Boudiaf
events.summary: The assassination of Mohamed Boudiaf took place on 29 June 1992. As Chairman of the High Council of Algeria, Boudiaf was killed by one of his own bodyguards, Lambarek Boumaarafi, who was presented officially as an Islamic fundamentalist, and a sympathiser of the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), who acted alone.

events.title: Planned Parenthood v. Casey
events.summary: Planned Parenthood v. Casey, 505 U.S. 833 (1992), was a landmark decision of the United States Supreme Court in which the Court upheld the right to have an abortion as established by the "essential holding" of Roe v.

events.title: Jan Stráský takes power
events.summary: Jan Stráský was a Czech politician. He served as the last prime minister of Czechoslovakia in 1992.

events.title: 18th G7 summit
events.summary: The 18th G7 Summit was held in Munich, Germany between 6 and 8 July 1992. The venue for the summit meetings was at the Residenz palace in central Munich.

events.title: 1992 Democratic Party presidential primaries
events.summary: From February 10 to June 9, 1992, voters of the Democratic Party chose its nominee for president in the 1992 United States presidential election.

events.title: Bordeaux Congress
events.summary: The Bordeaux Congress was the fifteenth national congress of the French Socialist Party. It took place from 10 to 12 July 1992.

events.title: Yitzhak Rabin takes power
events.summary: Yitzhak Rabin was an Israeli statesman and general who was the prime minister of Israel, having served from 1974 to 1977 and again from 1992 until his assassination in 1995. He was the first prime minister to have been born in the region of Palestine, at the time under British control.

events.title: 1992 Labour Party leadership election
events.summary: The 1992 Labour Party leadership election followed the Labour Party's failure to win the 1992 general election and the subsequent resignation of party leader Neil Kinnock.

events.title: Terrorist attack: Via D'Amelio bombing
events.summary: The via D'Amelio bombing was a terrorist attack by the Sicilian Mafia, which took place in Palermo, Sicily, Italy, on 19 July 1992. It killed Paolo Borsellino, the anti-Mafia Italian magistrate, and five members of his police escort: Agostino Catalano, Emanuela Loi, Vincenzo Li Muli, Walter Eddie Cosina, and Claudio Traina.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Bosnia-Herzegovina vs Croatian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina (Croat)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina over control of Croat, starting 1992-07-21. This episode was active in 3 years (1992–1994), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-03-16.

events.title: 1992 Croatian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Croatia for the first time on 2 August 1992 alongside simultaneous parliamentary elections. The result was a victory for incumbent Franjo Tuđman of the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), who received 58% of the vote, becoming the first popularly elected president of Croatia. Voter turnout was 75%.

events.title: 1992 Croatian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Croatia on 2 August 1992, alongside presidential elections. They were the first elections after independence and under the new constitution. All 138 seats in the Chamber of Representatives were up for election. The result was a victory for the Croatian Democratic Union, which won an absolute majority of 85 seats.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Papua New Guinea vs BRA (Bougainville)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Papua New Guinea and BRA over control of Bougainville, starting 1992-08-02. This episode was active in 5 years (1992–1996), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1996-11-28.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs NSCN-IM (Nagaland)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and NSCN-IM over control of Nagaland, starting 1992-08-05. This episode was active in 6 years (1992–1997), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1997-07-22.

events.title: Natural disaster: Hurricane Andrew
events.summary: Hurricane Andrew was a compact but extremely powerful tropical cyclone that became the most destructive hurricane to ever hit Florida in terms of structures damaged or destroyed and remained the costliest in financial terms until Hurricane Irma surpassed it 25 years later.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Georgia vs Republic of Abkhazia (Abkhazia)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Georgia and Republic of Abkhazia over control of Abkhazia, starting 1992-08-17. This episode was active in 2 years (1992–1993), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-11-29.

events.title: Branko Crvenkovski takes power
events.summary: Branko Crvenkovski is a Macedonian politician who served as the President of Macedonia from 2004 to 2009. He previously served as Prime Minister of Macedonia from 1992 to 1998 and from 2002 to 2004.

events.title: 1992 Bahamian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in the Bahamas on 19 August 1992. The result was a victory for the opposition Free National Movement (FNM), which received 55% of the vote and won 33 of the 49 seats in the House of Assembly, while the ruling Progressive Liberal Party (PLP) lost nearly half their seats, winning only 16.

events.title: Hubert Ingraham takes power
events.summary: Hubert Alexander Ingraham, PC is a Bahamian politician who was Prime Minister of The Bahamas from August 1992 to May 2002, and again from May 2007 to May 2012. He is a member of the Free National Movement Party (FNM). Prior to the 2012 election, he was the FNM's Party Leader and member of Parliament for the North Abaco constituency.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Senegal vs MFDC (Casamance)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Senegal and MFDC over control of Casamance, starting 1992-09-01. This episode was active in 2 years (1992–1993), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-11-16.

events.title: 1992 Djiboutian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Djibouti on 4 September 1992. The new constitution would restore multi-party democracy for the first time since independence. A second question asked voters whether the number of political parties should be limited to four. Both were approved by over 97.9% of voters with a 75.2% turnout.

events.title: 1992 Estonian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Estonia alongside presidential elections on 20 September 1992, the first after regaining independence from the Soviet Union. The newly elected 101 members of the 7th Riigikogu assembled at Toompea Castle in Tallinn within ten days of the election.

events.title: 1992 French Maastricht Treaty referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the Maastricht Treaty for the founding of the European Union was held in France on 20 September 1992. It was approved by 51% of the voters.

events.title: Treaty signed: OSPAR Convention
events.summary: The Convention for the Protection of the Marine Environment of the North-East Atlantic or OSPAR Convention is the current legislative instrument regulating international cooperation on environmental protection in the North-East Atlantic.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Myanmar vs KNPP (Karenni)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Myanmar (Burma) and KNPP over control of Karenni, starting 1992-09-22. This episode was active in 1 year (1992–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-11-06.

events.title: 1992 Romanian parliamentary election
events.summary: General elections were held in Romania on 27 September 1992, with a second round of the presidential election on 11 October. They were the first held after the adoption of a permanent constitution via a referendum held the previous winter.

events.title: 1992 Czechoslovak presidential election
events.summary: The 1992 Czechoslovak presidential election was held from July to October 1992, but parliament failed to elect a new president, foreshadowing the breakup of Czechoslovakia. Incumbent President Václav Havel participated in the first ballot held on 3 July 1992. He ran unopposed but failed to receive enough votes from Slovak MPs to be re-elected.

events.title: 1992 Estonian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Estonia on 20 September 1992, alongside parliamentary elections. As no candidate received over 50% of the vote, a second round was held in Parliament on 5 October 1992, in which Lennart Meri was elected. Voter turnout in the public vote was 68%.

events.title: 1992 Georgian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Georgia on 11 October 1992, in which voters elected both the Parliament and the Chairman of Parliament, who also acted as Head of State as the President, Zviad Gamsakhurdia, was in exile after being ousted in a coup in January.

events.title: 1992 Romanian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Romania on 27 September 1992, with a second round of the presidential election on 11 October. They were the first held after the adoption of a permanent constitution via a referendum held the previous winter.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs ATTF (Tripura)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and ATTF over control of Tripura, starting 1992-10-12. This episode was active in 1 year (1992–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-12-31.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: United Kingdom.

events.title: 1992 Lithuanian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A referendum on a new constitution was held in Lithuania on 25 October 1992, alongside the first round of parliamentary elections. It was approved by 78.2% of those voting and 56.8% of all registered voters, passing the 50% threshold.

events.title: Mart Laar takes power
events.summary: Mart Laar is an Estonian politician and historian. He served as the Prime Minister of Estonia from 1992 to 1994 and from 1999 to 2002. Laar is credited with having helped bring about Estonia's rapid economic development during the 1990s. He is a member of the centre-right Isamaa party.

events.title: 1992 United States presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in the United States on November 3, 1992. The Democratic ticket of Arkansas governor Bill Clinton and Tennessee junior senator Al Gore defeated incumbent Republican president George H. W. Bush and vice president Dan Quayle and the independent ticket of businessman Ross Perot and vice admiral James Stockdale.

events.title: Treaty signed: European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages
events.summary: The European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages (ECRML) is a European treaty adopted in 1992 under the auspices of the Council of Europe to protect and promote historical regional and minority languages in Europe.

events.title: 1992 Lithuanian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Lithuania in two stages on 25 October and 15 November 1992. A total of 141 members were elected to the Seimas, which replaced the Supreme Council; 70 were elected using proportional representation and 71 from single-member constituencies.

events.title: 1992 Panamanian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Panama on November 15, 1992. Voters were asked whether they approved of a series of amendments to the 1972 constitution, including reducing the power of the armed forces. Only 32.83% voted in favour of the reforms, with a turnout of 40%.

events.title: 1992 Irish general election
events.summary: The 1992 Irish general election to the 27th Dáil was held on Wednesday, 25 November, almost three weeks after the dissolution of the 26th Dáil on 5 November by President Mary Robinson, on the request of Taoiseach Albert Reynolds following a defeat of the government in a motion of confidence.

events.title: Fourteenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
events.summary: Three referendums were held in Ireland on 25 November 1992, the same day as the 1992 general election. Each was on a proposed amendment of the Irish constitution relating to the law on abortion. They were enumerated as the Twelfth, Thirteenth and Fourteenth Amendments.

events.title: Thirteenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
events.summary: Three referendums were held in Ireland on 25 November 1992, the same day as the 1992 general election. Each was on a proposed amendment of the Irish constitution relating to the law on abortion. They were enumerated as the Twelfth, Thirteenth and Fourteenth Amendments.

events.title: Twelfth Amendment of the Constitution Bill 1992
events.summary: Three referendums were held in Ireland on 25 November 1992, the same day as the 1992 general election. Each was on a proposed amendment of the Irish constitution relating to the law on abortion. They were enumerated as the Twelfth, Thirteenth and Fourteenth Amendments.

events.title: Algirdas Brazauskas takes power
events.summary: Algirdas Mykolas Brazauskas was the fourth president of Lithuania, in office from 1993 to 1998. He also served as Prime Minister of Lithuania from 2001 to 2006. Brazauskas was the first democratically elected president of post-Soviet Lithuania.

events.title: Demolition of the Babri Masjid
events.summary: The Babri Masjid, a 16th-century mosque in the Indian city of Ayodhya, was destroyed on 6 December 1992 by a large group of activists of the Vishva Hindu Parishad and allied organisations. The mosque had been the subject of a lengthy socio-political dispute, and was targeted after a political rally organised by Hindu nationalist organisations turned violent.

events.title: 1992 Slovenian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Slovenia on 6 December 1992. The result was a victory for incumbent Milan Kučan, who won 63.93% of the vote. Voter turnout was 85.78%.

events.title: 1992 Slovenian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Slovenia on 6 and 10 December 1992. These were the first legislative elections to the National Assembly after the rename of the Assembly of the Republic of Slovenia in December 1991 and the first elections in independent Slovenia. The result was a victory for the Liberal Democratic Party, which won 22 of the 90 seats.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: United Kingdom.

events.title: 1992 Uruguayan privatisation referendum
events.summary: A referendum on partially repealing the law on public enterprises was held in Uruguay on 13 December 1992. The proposed repeal was approved by 73% of voters.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Indonesia vs CNRT (East Timor)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Indonesia and CNRT over control of East Timor, starting 1992-12-15. This episode was active in 1 year (1992–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-12-15.

events.title: 1992 Serbian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Serbia on 20 December 1992. The vote was held only two years after the previous election and as a result of a referendum which approved holding early elections.

events.title: Serbian parliamentary election, 1992
events.summary: General elections were held in Serbia on 20 December 1992. The vote was held only two years after the previous election and as a result of a referendum which approved holding early elections.

events.title: 1992 Nigerien constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Niger on 26 December 1992. The new constitution would restore multi-party democracy for the first time since 1960, whilst also allowing unlimited number of five-year terms for the President. It was approved by 89.79% of voters, with a turnout of 56.6%.

events.title: Lyuben Berov takes power
events.summary: Lyuben Borisov Berov was a Bulgarian economist who served as the Prime Minister of Bulgaria from 1992 to 1994. A political independent, he previously held the role of an economic adviser to President Zhelyu Zhelev.

events.title: Josef Klaus takes power
events.summary: Josef Klaus was an Austrian politician of the conservative People's Party (ÖVP). He served as State Governor (Landeshauptmann) of Salzburg from 1949 to 1961, as Minister of Finance from 1961 to 1963 and as Chancellor of Austria from 1964 to 1970.

events.title: Vladimír Mečiar takes power
events.summary: Vladimír Mečiar is a Slovak former politician who served as the prime minister of Slovakia from June 1990 to May 1991, June 1992 to March 1994, and again from December 1994 to October 1998. He was the leader of the Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), a populist party in Slovakia.

events.title: Adolf Ogi takes power
events.summary: Adolf Ogi is a Swiss politician who most recently served as Special Advisor to the UN Secretary General on Sport for Development and Peace from 2001 to 2008. He previously served as member of the Federal Council (Switzerland) for the Swiss People's Party from 1987 to 2000. He held the Presidency of the Swiss Confederation twice in 1993 and 2000.

events.title: Treaty signed: START II
events.summary: START II was a bilateral treaty between the United States and Russia on the Reduction and Limitation of Strategic Offensive Arms. It was signed by US president George H. W. Bush and Russian president Boris Yeltsin on 3 January 1993, banning the use of multiple independently targetable re-entry vehicles (MIRVs) on intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs).

events.title: Treaty signed: Chemical Weapons Convention
events.summary: The Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC), officially the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction, is an arms control treaty administered by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), an intergovernmental organization based in The Hague, Netherlands.

events.title: Bill Clinton takes power
events.summary: William Jefferson Clinton is an American retired politician and lawyer who served as the 42nd president of the United States from 1993 to 2001. A member of the Democratic Party, he previously served as the attorney general of Arkansas from 1977 to 1979, the governor of Arkansas from 1979 to 1981, and governor again from 1983 to 1992.

events.title: First inauguration of Bill Clinton
events.summary: The first inauguration of Bill Clinton as the 42nd president of the United States was held on Wednesday, January 20, 1993, at the West Front of the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C. This was the 52nd inauguration and marked the commencement of the first term of Bill Clinton as president and Al Gore as vice president.

events.title: Battle: Operation Maslenica
events.summary: Operation Maslenica was a Croatian Army offensive launched in January 1993 to retake territory in northern Dalmatia and Lika from Krajina Serb forces, with the stated military objective of pushing the Serbs back from approaches to Zadar, Maslenica and Karlobag, allowing a secure land route between Dalmatia and northern Croatia to be opened.

events.title: 1993 Monegasque general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Monaco on 24 January 1993, with a second round of voting on 31 January. The result was a victory for the National and Democratic Union, which won 15 of the 18 seats in the National Council, the first time since 1973 that it had failed to win all 18 seats.

events.title: Poul Nyrup Rasmussen takes power
events.summary: Poul Oluf Nyrup Rasmussen is a retired Danish politician, who served as Prime Minister of Denmark from 25 January 1993 to 27 November 2001 and President of the Party of European Socialists (PES) from 2004 to 2011. He was the leader of the governing Social Democrats from 1992 to 2002 and was also a member of the European Parliament from 2004 to 2009.

events.title: 1993 Czech presidential election
events.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in the Czech Republic on 26 January 1993 to elect the first president of the newly independent country. The president was elected by the members of the Czech Republic Parliament, with Václav Havel emerging as the winner.

events.title: February 1993 Liechtenstein general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Liechtenstein on 7 February 1993 to elect the 25 members of the Landtag. The Progressive Citizens' Party (FBP) won a plurality of twelve seats, with the Patriotic Union (VU) winning eleven. The Free List (FL) won two seats, which was the first time a third party won seats in the Landtag. Voter turnout was 87.5%.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Philippines vs ASG, MNLF (Mindanao)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Philippines and ASG, MNLF over control of Mindanao, starting 1993-02-09. This episode was active in 28 years (1993–2020), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 2020-12-09.

events.title: 1993 Cypriot presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Cyprus on 7 February 1993, with a second round on 14 February. The result was a victory for Glafcos Clerides of the Democratic Rally after he finished as runner-up behind George Vassiliou, supported by AKEL, in the first round, a reverse of the 1988 elections.

events.title: 1993 Lithuanian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Lithuania on 14 February 1993. They were the first presidential elections under the new October 1992 constitution and the first direct presidential elections in the country's history.

events.title: 1993 Slovak presidential election
events.summary: The 1993 Slovak presidential elections were held between 26 January and 15 February 1993. Michal Kováč was elected as the first president of Slovakia and became the only Slovak president elected by Parliament. A candidate needed to receive 90 votes to be elected.

events.title: 1993 Cuban parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Cuba on 24 February 1993 alongside elections to the fourteen Provincial Assemblies. Following the implementation of a new electoral law in 1992, voters now elected the National Assembly directly. Previously voters had elected members of the country's 169 municipal assemblies, who in turn had elected the National Assembly.

events.title: Terrorist attack: 1993 World Trade Center bombing
events.summary: On February 26, 1993, Ramzi Yousef and associates carried out a van bomb terrorist attack below the North Tower of the World Trade Center in New York City.

events.title: Glafcos Clerides takes power
events.summary: Glafcos Ioannou Clerides was a Cypriot statesman who served as President of Cyprus in 1974 and from 1993 to 2003.

events.title: 1993 Liechtenstein public buildings referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the construction of public buildings was held in Liechtenstein on 7 March 1993. Voters were asked whether they approved of the construction of a new main building and some annexes for the Liechtenstein parliament, Landtag. The proposal was rejected by 79.6% of voters.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Egypt vs al-Gama'a al-Islamiyya
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Egypt and al-Gama'a al-Islamiyya over control of the government, starting 1993-03-10. This episode was active in 6 years (1993–1998), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1998-11-02.

events.title: Terrorist attack: 1993 Bombay bombings
events.summary: The 1993 Bombay bombings was a series of 12 terrorist bombings in Bombay, Maharashtra, on 12 March 1993. The single-day attacks resulted in 257 fatalities and 1,400 injuries. The bombings took place in the aftermath of the Bombay riots, which themselves had followed the demolition of the five-century-old Babri Masjid in Ayodhya by a Hindutva mob.

events.title: 1993 Andorran constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Andorra on 14 March 1993. Drafted by the Co-Princes and the General Council, the new constitution was approved by 74.2% of voters, with a 76% turnout. The first elections under the new constitution were held later in the year.

events.title: 1993 Israeli presidential election
events.summary: An election for President of Israel was held in the Knesset on 24 March 1993, following the end of Chaim Herzog's second five-year term in office.

events.title: Battle of Kalbajar
events.summary: The Battle of Kalbajar took place in March and April 1993, during the First Nagorno-Karabakh War. It resulted in the capture of the Kalbajar District of Azerbaijan by Armenian military forces.

events.title: 1993 French legislative election
events.summary: Legislative elections were held in France on 21 and 28 March 1993, to elect the tenth National Assembly of the Fifth Republic.

events.title: 1993 Jamaican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Jamaica on 30 March 1993. The result was a victory for the People's National Party, which won 52 of the 60 seats. Voter turnout was 67%.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Iran vs MEK
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Iran and MEK over control of the government, starting 1993-04-09. This episode was active in 1 year (1993–1993), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-12-11.

events.title: Assassination of Guillem Agulló
events.summary: Guillem Agulló i Salvador was a Valencian anti-fascist and pro-Catalan independence young activist who was assassinated on 11 April 1993, by the Spanish neo-Nazi Pedro Cuevas, in Montanejos. His assassination is a famous case in the Catalan-speaking countries, where Agulló has become a symbol of anti-fascism and anti-racism.

events.title: 1993 Brazilian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Brazil on 21 April 1993 to determine the form of government of the country. After the re-democratization of Brazil, an article in the new Constitution determined the holding of a referendum for voters to decide if the country should remain a republic or become a monarchy again, and if the system of government should…

events.title: Terrorist attack: 1993 Bishopsgate bombing
events.summary: On 24 April 1993, the Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) detonated a powerful truck bomb on Bishopsgate, a major thoroughfare in London's financial district, the City of London.

events.title: 1993 Eritrean independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in Eritrea, at the time part of Ethiopia, between 23 and 25 April 1993. The result was 99.83% in favour, with a turnout in excess of 98%. Independence from Ethiopia was declared on 27 April 1993.

events.title: 1993 Russian government referendum
events.summary: A four-part referendum was held in Russia on 25 April 1993. Voters were asked questions on confidence in President Boris Yeltsin, support for the government's socio-economic policies and early elections for both the presidency and parliament.

events.title: Carlo Azeglio Ciampi takes power
events.summary: Carlo Azeglio Ciampi was an Italian politician, statesman and banker who was the president of Italy from 1999 to 2006 and prime minister of Italy from 1993 to 1994.

events.title: 1993 San Marino general election
events.summary: General elections were held in San Marino on 13 May 1993. The Sammarinese Christian Democratic Party remained the largest party, winning 26 of the 60 seats in the Grand and General Council, and continued their coalition with the Sammarinese Socialist Party.

events.title: 1993 Republika Srpska referendum
events.summary: A two-part referendum was held in Republika Srpska on 15 and 16 May 1993. Voters were asked whether they approved of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, and whether Republika Srpska should be able to join another country.

events.title: Erdal İnönü takes power
events.summary: Erdal İnönü was a Turkish theoretical physicist and politician who served as the interim prime minister of Turkey between 16 May and 25 June 1993. He also served as the deputy prime minister of Turkey from 1991 to 1993 and as the minister of foreign affairs from March to October 1995.

events.title: 1993 Turkish presidential election
events.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in Turkey in May 1993 to elect the country's ninth president, who would succeed Turgut Özal who had recently died. The candidate of DYP was Süleyman Demirel who was also supported by SHP. In the first and second rounds, the ruling party DYP was unsuccessful in electing its candidate, Süleyman Demirel.

events.title: 1993 Danish Maastricht Treaty referendum
events.summary: A second referendum on the Maastricht Treaty was held in Denmark on 18 May 1993. After rejecting the treaty in a referendum the previous year, this time it was approved by 56.7% of voters with an 86.5% turnout.

events.title: Terrorist attack: 1993 Solingen arson attack
events.summary: The Solingen arson attack was one of the most severe instances of racist violence in modern Germany. On the night of 28–29 May 1993, four young German men belonging to the far right skinhead scene, with neo-Nazi ties, set fire to the house of a large Turkish family in the city of Solingen, in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

events.title: Gustavo Adolfo Espina Salguero takes power
events.summary: Gustavo Adolfo Espina Salguero was a Guatemalan politician who served as vice president from 1991 to 1993 under President Jorge Serrano and later Acting President for 4 days during the 1993 Guatemalan constitutional crisis.

events.title: Ramiro de León Carpio takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: Ramiro de León Carpio was a Guatemalan politician who served as the 43rd president of Guatemala from June 1993 until January 1996. He served as Guatemala's Attorney for Human Rights from August 1987 to June 1993.

events.title: 1993 Guatemalan presidential election
events.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in Guatemala on 5 June 1993. They were sparked by the 1993 Guatemalan constitutional crisis in which President Jorge Serrano Elías had attempted a self-coup.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Azerbaijan vs Military faction (forces of Suret Husseinov)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Azerbaijan and Military faction (forces of Suret Husseinov) over control of the government, starting 1993-06-06. This episode was active in 1 year (1993–1993), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-06-15.

events.title: 1993 Latvian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Latvia on 5 and 6 June 1993, the first after independence was restored in 1991. Latvian Way emerged as the largest party in the Saeima, winning 36 of the 100 seats. A total of 23 parties participated in the elections, although only eight received 4% or more of votes and won seats.

events.title: 1993 Spanish general election
events.summary: A general election was held in Spain on 6 June 1993 to elect the members of the 5th Cortes Generales under the Spanish Constitution of 1978. All 350 seats in the Congress of Deputies were up for election, as well as 208 of 256 seats in the Senate.

events.title: 1993 Malawian democracy referendum
events.summary: A referendum on reintroducing multi-party democracy was held in Malawi on 14 June 1993. It asked voters to decide whether Malawi would remain a single-party state or transition to a multiparty democracy.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Denmark.

events.title: Heydar Aliyev takes power
events.summary: Heydar Alirza oghlu Aliyev was an Azerbaijani politician who was a Soviet party boss in the Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic from 1969 to 1982, and the third president of Azerbaijan from 1993 to 2003.

events.title: Kim Campbell takes power
events.summary: Avril Phaedra Douglas "Kim" Campbell is a Canadian politician who was the 19th prime minister of Canada from June to November 1993. Campbell is the first and only female prime minister of Canada.

events.title: Tansu Çiller takes power
events.summary: Tansu Çiller is a Turkish academic, economist, and politician who served as the 22nd prime minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996. She is Turkey's only female prime minister. As the leader of the True Path Party, she went on to concurrently serve as Deputy Prime Minister of Turkey and as minister of foreign affairs between 1996 and 1997.

events.title: 1993 Belizean general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Belize on 30 June 1993. Although the People's United Party received the most votes, the United Democratic Party–National Alliance for Belizean Rights alliance won the most seats. Voter turnout was 72%.

events.title: Manuel Esquivel takes power
events.summary: Sir Manuel Amadeo Esquivel was a Belizean politician. As leader of the United Democratic Party, he served as the second prime minister of Belize from 1984 to 1989, and then again from 1993 to 1998. His party's victory in 1984 was the first time an opposition party had won a general election in Belize.

events.title: Blaga Dimitrova resigns as Vice President of Bulgaria
events.summary: Blaga Dimitrova resigned as Vice President of Bulgaria on 6 July 1993, having held the office since 22 January 1992.

events.title: 19th G7 summit
events.summary: The 19th G7 Summit was held in Tokyo, Japan, on July 7–9, 1993. The venue for the summit meetings was the State Guesthouse in Tokyo, Japan.

events.title: 1993 Latvian presidential election
events.summary: The 1993 presidential elections in Latvia took place on July 7, 1993. It was the first presidential election after the restoration of Latvia's independence. Guntis Ulmanis was elected the 5th President of Latvia.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Myanmar vs MTA (Shan)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Myanmar (Burma) and MTA over control of Shan, starting 1993-07-16. This episode was active in 10 years (1993–2002), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2002-09-24.

events.title: 1993 Narva and Sillamäe autonomy referendum
events.summary: The 1993 Narva and Sillamäe autonomy referendum was an unconstitutional referendum held on 16–17 July 1993 in Narva and Sillamäe in north-east Estonia, on whether to seek autonomy within the country.

events.title: Valdis Birkavs takes power
events.summary: Valdis Birkavs is a Latvian politician. He was born in Riga. Birkavs attended the University of Latvia, where he studied philosophy, sociology, law, psychology and mathematical logic. He was first elected to the Latvian parliament in 1990 and helped to found the Latvian Way party.

events.title: Treaty signed: Arusha Accords (Rwanda)
events.summary: The Arusha Accords, officially the Peace Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Rwanda and the Rwandan Patriotic Front, also known as the Arusha Peace Agreement or Arusha negotiations, were a set of five accords signed in Arusha, Tanzania, on 4 August 1993, by the government of Rwanda and the rebel Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF), under…

events.title: Morihiro Hosokawa takes power
events.summary: Morihiro Hosokawa is a Japanese politician who served as prime minister of Japan from 1993 to 1994. He led an eight-party coalition government which was the first Japanese government not headed by a Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) premier since 1955.

events.title: 1993 Azerbaijani vote of confidence referendum
events.summary: A national vote of confidence in President Abulfaz Elchibey was held in Azerbaijan on 29 August 1993, following a coup d'état in June by Surat Huseynov. Voters were asked if they trusted the President of the Azerbaijan Republic. Only 2% of voters voted "yes", with turnout reported to be 92%. Elchibey was formally removed from office on 1 September.

events.title: Coup: 1993 Azerbaijani coup d'état
events.summary: The 1993 Azeri coup d'état, also known as the Ganja Uprising, was a military coup led by Azerbaijani military commander Surat Huseynov.

events.title: Battle: Operation Medak Pocket
events.summary: Operation Medak Pocket, officially called by Croatians Operation Pocket-93 (Operacija Džep-93) was a military operation undertaken by the Croatian Army between 9 – 17 September 1993, in which a salient reaching the south suburbs of Gospić, in the south-central Lika region of Croatia then under the control of the self-proclaimed Republic of Serbian Krajina,…

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Iran vs KDPI (Kurdistan)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Iran and KDPI over control of Kurdistan, starting 1993-09-12. This episode was active in 1 year (1993–1993), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-11-11.

events.title: Oslo I Accord
events.summary: The Oslo I Accord or Oslo I, officially called the Declaration of Principles on Interim Self-Government Arrangements or short Declaration of Principles (DOP), was an attempt in 1993 to set up a framework that would lead to the resolution of the ongoing Israeli–Palestinian conflict.

events.title: 1993 Norwegian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Norway on 12 and 13 September 1993. It was the first European election where the two largest parties fielded a female leadership candidate, and the first election in history where all the largest three parties fielded female leadership candidates.

events.title: 1993 Polish parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Poland on 19 September 1993. All 460 members of the Sejm and 100 senators of the Senate were elected. The elections were won by the left-wing parties of the Democratic Left Alliance and the Polish People's Party, who formed a coalition government. The coalition was just four seats short of a supermajority.

events.title: 1993 Azerbaijani presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Azerbaijan on 3 October 1993, nearly four months after the June 1993 coup d'état. The result was a victory for incumbent president Heydar Aliyev of the New Azerbaijan Party, who won with nearly 99% of the vote. Election monitors characterized the elections as neither free nor fair.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Bosnia-Herzegovina vs Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia (Bihaca Krajina)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia over control of Bihaca Krajina, starting 1993-10-03. This episode was active in 3 years (1993–1995), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1995-07-28.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Russia vs Parliamentary Forces
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Russia (Soviet Union) and Parliamentary Forces over control of the government, starting 1993-10-03. This episode was active in 1 year (1993–1993), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-10-05.

events.title: Battle of Mogadishu (1993)
events.summary: The Battle of Mogadishu, also known as the Black Hawk Down Incident, was part of Operation Gothic Serpent. It was fought on 3–4 October 1993, in Mogadishu, Somalia, between forces of the United States—supported by UNOSOM II—against Somali National Alliance (SNA) fighters and other insurgents in south Mogadishu.

events.title: 1993 Egyptian presidential confirmation referendum
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Egypt on 4 October 1993. The vote took the form of a referendum on the candidacy of Hosni Mubarak after he was nominated for the post by a 439–9 vote in the People's Assembly on 21 July. His candidacy for a third consecutive six-year term was allegedly approved by 96.3% of voters, with a turnout of 84.2%.

events.title: 1993 Greek parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Greece on 10 October 1993. PASOK of Andreas Papandreou, was elected with 170 of the 300 seats, defeating the liberal-conservative New Democracy party of Konstantinos Mitsotakis.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ethiopia vs AIAI (Ogaden)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Ethiopia and AIAI over control of Ogaden, starting 1993-10-13. This episode was active in 2 years (1993–1994), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-02-26.

events.title: Andreas Papandreou takes power
events.summary: Andreas Georgiou Papandreou was a Greek academic and economist who was prime minister of Greece from 1981 to 1989 and again from 1993 to 1996. He founded PASOK, the Panhellenic Socialist Movement.

events.title: Coup: 1993 Burundian coup attempt
events.summary: On 21 October 1993, a coup was attempted in Burundi by a Tutsi–dominated army faction. The coup attempt resulted in assassination of Hutu President Melchior Ndadaye and the deaths of other officials in the constitutional line of presidential succession.

events.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 1993
events.summary: The 1993 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting was the 13th Meeting of the Heads of Government of the Commonwealth of Nations. It was held in Limassol, Cyprus, between 21 October 1993 and 25 October 1993, and was hosted by Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides.

events.title: Terrorist attack: Shankill Road bombing
events.summary: The Shankill Road bombing was carried out by the Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) on 23 October 1993 and is one of the most well-known incidents of the Troubles in Northern Ireland.

events.title: October 1993 Liechtenstein general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Liechtenstein on 24 October 1993 to elect the 25 members of the Landtag. Early elections were called following prime minister Markus Büchel being subject to a successful motion of no confidence at the request of his own party, the Progressive Citizens' Party (FBP).

events.title: 1993 Canadian federal election
events.summary: The 1993 Canadian federal election was held on October 25, 1993, to elect members to the House of Commons of the 35th Parliament of Canada. Considered to be a major political realignment, it was one of the most eventful elections in Canada's history. Two new regionalist parties emerged, finishing second and third in seat count.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Belgium.

events.title: 1993 Peruvian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Peru on 31 October 1993. It followed Alberto Fujimori's presidential coup on 5 April 1992. A new constitution was published on 4 September 1993, limiting the President to two terms of five years, creating a unicameral Congress.

events.title: Jean Chrétien takes power
events.summary: Joseph Jacques Jean Chrétien is a Canadian lawyer and former politician who served as the 20th prime minister of Canada from 1993 to 2003. He served as leader of the Liberal Party from 1990 to 2003 and as leader of the Official Opposition from 1990 to 1993.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Congo vs Ninjas
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Congo and Ninjas over control of the government, starting 1993-11-11. This episode was active in 1 year (1993–1993), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-12-27.

events.title: 1993 Puerto Rican status referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the political status of the archipelago and island was held in Puerto Rico on 14 November 1993. Voters were given the choice between being a Commonwealth, statehood or independence. A plurality of voters voted for Commonwealth status, with a voter turnout of 73.5%.

events.title: 1993 Curaçao status referendum
events.summary: A status referendum was held on the island of Curaçao on 19 November 1993. The referendum was the result of a discussion about the future of the Netherlands Antilles, following the secession of Aruba in 1986.

events.title: 1993 Honduran general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Honduras on 27 November 1993. Voters cast a single ballot for both the presidential and Congressional election.

events.title: 1993 Saint Kitts and Nevis general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Saint Kitts and Nevis on 29 November 1993. No party won a majority, and although the Saint Kitts and Nevis Labour Party received the most votes, the People's Action Movement remained in power in a minority cabinet in coalition with Nevis Reformation Party.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Belgium.

events.title: 1993 Andorran parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Andorra on 12 December 1993. Following the adoption of a new constitution by a referendum earlier in the year, they were the first elections in which political parties were allowed to run.

events.title: Péter Boross takes power
events.summary: Péter Boross is a Hungarian retired politician and former member of the Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF) who served as Prime Minister of Hungary from December 1993 to July 1994.

events.title: 1993 Russian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Russia on 12 December 1993. The new constitution was approved by 58% of voters, and came into force on 25 December.

events.title: 1993 Russian legislative election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Russia on 12 December 1993 to elect all 450 seats of the 1st State Duma of the Russian Federation. Additionally, the elections were the first and only instance of direct elections to the Federation Council, with future members appointed by provincial legislatures and governors.

events.title: 1993 Serbian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Yugoslav republic of Serbia on 19 December 1993, to elect members of the National Assembly. The Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) of Slobodan Milošević emerged as the largest party in the National Assembly, winning 123 of the 250 seats.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs UNLF (Manipur)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and UNLF over control of Manipur, starting 1993-12-31. This episode was active in 4 years (1993–1996), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1996-12-19.

events.title: Treaty signed: North American Free Trade Agreement
events.summary: The North American Free Trade Agreement, referred to colloquially in the Anglosphere as NAFTA, was an agreement signed by Canada, Mexico, and the United States that created a trilateral trade bloc in North America.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Mexico vs EZLN
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Mexico and EZLN over control of the government, starting 1994-01-01. This episode was active in 1 year (1994–1994), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-02-23.

events.title: 1994 Brussels NATO summit
events.summary: The 1994 Brussels summit was the 13th NATO summit bringing the leaders of member nations together at the same time. The formal sessions and informal meetings in Brussels, Belgium took place on 10–11 January 1994.

events.title: 1994 Turkmen presidential term referendum
events.summary: A referendum on extending President Saparmurat Niyazov's term until 2002 was held in Turkmenistan on 15 January 1994. Official results showed that the proposal was approved by 99.99% of voters with a 100% turnout.

events.title: Earthquake: 1994 Northridge earthquake
events.summary: The 1994 Northridge earthquake affected Greater Los Angeles, California, United States, on January 17, 1994, at 04:30:55 PST. The epicenter of the moment magnitude 6.7 blind thrust earthquake was beneath the San Fernando Valley. The shock lasted approximately 8 seconds and achieved a peak ground acceleration of over 1.7 g.

events.title: Carlos Roberto Reina takes power
events.summary: Carlos Roberto Reina Idiáquez was a Honduran politician, lawyer and diplomat who served as the President of Honduras from 1994 to 1998. He was a member of the Honduran Liberal Party.

events.title: Myechyslaw Hryb takes power
events.summary: Myechyslaw Ivanavich Hryb is a Belarusian politician who was the second head of state of Belarus from January to July 1994 and the second chairman of the Supreme Council of Belarus from 1994 to 1996.

events.title: 1994 Guatemalan constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Guatemala on 30 January 1994. It followed a constitutional crisis and an attempted self-coup on 25 May 1993 by President Jorge Serrano Elías. Among the reforms was a plan to reduce the parliamentary term of the current government. The changes were approved by 83.9% of voters, although voter turnout was just 15.9%.

events.title: 1994 Kyrgyz presidential referendum
events.summary: A referendum on President Askar Akayev was held in Kyrgyzstan on 30 January 1994. Voters were asked "Do you confirm that the President of Kyrgyzstan who was democratically elected on 12 October 1991 for 5 years is the President of the Kyrgyz Republic with the right to act as head of state during his term in office?" The result was 97% in favour, with…

events.title: Costa Rican parliamentary election, 1994
events.summary: General elections were held in Costa Rica on 6 February 1994. José María Figueres of the National Liberation Party won the presidential election, whilst his party also won the parliamentary election. Voter turnout was 81%.

events.title: 1994 Costa Rican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Costa Rica on 6 February 1994. José María Figueres of the National Liberation Party won the presidential election, whilst his party also won the parliamentary election. Voter turnout was 81%.

events.title: 1994 Finnish presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Finland on 16 January 1994, with a second round on 6 February. It was the first time the President had been solely and directly elected by a popular vote. Martti Ahtisaari defeated Elisabeth Rehn in the second round.

events.title: 1994 Vincentian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines on 21 February 1994. The result was a victory for the New Democratic Party, which won twelve of the fifteen seats. Voter turnout was 66%.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Uganda vs LRA
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Uganda and LRA over control of the government, starting 1994-02-21. This episode was active in 18 years (1994–2011), 3 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 2011-11-03.

events.title: 1994 Moldovan parliamentary election
events.summary: Early parliamentary elections were held in Moldova on 27 February 1994. They were the country's first competitive elections, and followed deadlock in Parliament over the issue of joining the Commonwealth of Independent States. The result was a victory for the Democratic Agrarian Party of Moldova (PDAM), which won 56 of the 104 seats.

events.title: Battle: 1994 Serb J-21 Jastreb shootdown
events.summary: On 28 February 1994, two pairs of North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) General Dynamics F-16C Fighting Falcon aircraft shot down five J-21 Jastreb single-seat light attack jets–piloted by Republika Srpska (RS) or Republic of Serbian Krajina (RSK) personnel–in Bosnia and Herzegovina airspace after they had bombed an armaments factory at Novi Travnik…

events.title: Martti Ahtisaari takes power
events.summary: Martti Oiva Kalevi Ahtisaari was a Finnish politician and diplomat who was the president of Finland from 1994 to 2000. He was Finland's Ambassador to Tanzania from 1973 to 1977 and United Nations Commissioner for Namibia from 1977 to 1981. Noted for his international peace work, he received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2008.

events.title: 1994 Moldovan referendum
events.summary: A referendum on remaining an independent nation was held in Moldova on 6 March 1994. Initiated by President Mircea Snegur, it was referred to as a "Consultation with the people", and was approved by 97.9% of voters.

events.title: 1994 Antiguan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Antigua and Barbuda on 8 March 1994. They were won by the governing Antigua Labour Party under the leadership of Lester Bird. Bird had been appointed leader of the ALP before the elections, after his father and predecessor Vere Bird announced his intention to retire. Lester Bird became Prime Minister after elections.

events.title: Jozef Moravčík takes power
events.summary: Jozef Moravčík is a Slovak diplomat and political figure. He served as the prime minister of Slovakia from 16 March 1994 to 13 December 1994, and later as the Mayor of Bratislava.

events.title: Treaty signed: Washington Agreement
events.summary: The Washington Agreement was a ceasefire agreement between the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia, signed on 18 March 1994 in Washington, D.C. It was signed by Bosnian Prime Minister Haris Silajdžić, Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granić and President of Herzeg-Bosnia Krešimir Zubak.

events.title: 1994 Salvadoran general election
events.summary: General elections were held in El Salvador on 20 March 1994, with a second round of the presidential elections taking place on 24 April. The president, vice president, 84 members of the National Assembly, and 262 mayors, were all up for election this cycle.

events.title: 1994 Italian general election
events.summary: The 1994 Italian general election was held on 27 and 28 March 1994 to elect members of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate of the Republic for the 12th legislature. Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right coalition won a large majority in the Chamber of Deputies but just missed winning a majority in the Senate.

events.title: 1994 Ukrainian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Ukraine on 27 March 1994, with a second round between 2 and 10 April. These were the first parliamentary elections in Ukraine as an independent state. A total of 15 political parties won seats, although a majority of deputies were independents.

events.title: 1994 Crimean referendum
events.summary: A three-part referendum was held in Crimea on 27 March 1994 alongside regional and national elections. Voters were asked whether they were in favour of greater autonomy within Ukraine, whether residents should have dual Russian and Ukrainian citizenship, and whether presidential decrees should have the status of laws. All three proposals were approved.

events.title: Rwandan genocide begins
events.summary: The Rwandan genocide, also known as the genocide against Tutsi, occurred from 7 April to 19 July 1994 during the Rwandan Civil War. Over a span of approximately 100 days, members of the Tutsi ethnic group, as well as some moderate Hutu and Twa, were systematically killed by Hutu militias.

events.title: Treaty signed: TRIPS Agreement
events.summary: The Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) is an international legal agreement between all the member nations of the World Trade Organization (WTO).

events.title: Tsutomu Hata takes power
events.summary: Tsutomu Hata was a Japanese politician who briefly served as prime minister of Japan in 1994.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Yemen vs Democratic Republic of Yemen (South Yemen)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Yemen (North Yemen) and Democratic Republic of Yemen over control of South Yemen, starting 1994-04-28. This episode was active in 1 year (1994–1994), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-07-04.

events.title: 1994 Dutch general election
events.summary: General elections were held in the Netherlands on 3 May 1994. The Labour Party emerged as the largest party, winning 37 of the 150 seats in the House of Representatives. The election resulted in significant losses for both the Labour Party and the Christian Democratic Appeal.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Pakistan vs MQM
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Pakistan and MQM over control of the government, starting 1994-05-03. This episode was active in 3 years (1994–1996), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1996-09-04.

events.title: Bishkek Protocol
events.summary: The Bishkek Protocol was a provisional ceasefire agreement, signed by the representatives of Armenia, Azerbaijan, the breakaway Republic of Artsakh, and Russia on May 12, 1994, in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan.

events.title: 1994 Panamanian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Panama on 8 May 1994, electing both a new President of the Republic and a new Legislative Assembly.

events.title: Silvio Berlusconi takes power
events.summary: Silvio Berlusconi was an Italian media tycoon and politician who served as the prime minister of Italy in three governments from 1994 to 1995, 2001 to 2006 and 2008 to 2011.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Myanmar vs RSO (Arakan)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Myanmar (Burma) and RSO over control of Arakan, starting 1994-05-15. This episode was active in 1 year (1994–1994), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-06-23.

events.title: 1994 Dominican Republic general election
events.summary: General elections were held in the Dominican Republic on 16 May 1994. Joaquín Balaguer of the Social Christian Reformist Party won the presidential election, whilst the Dominican Revolutionary Party-led alliance won the Congressional elections. Voter turnout was 87.6%.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Niger vs CRA (Air and Azawad)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Niger and CRA over control of Air and Azawad, starting 1994-05-16. This episode was active in 1 year (1994–1994), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-09-26.

events.title: 1994 Hungarian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Hungary on 8 May 1994, with a second round of voting in 174 of the 176 single member constituencies on 29 May. They resulted in the return to power of the Hungarian Socialist Party, the former Communist party, under the leadership of Gyula Horn, who became prime minister.

events.title: Armando Calderón Sol takes power
events.summary: Armando Calderón Sol was a Salvadoran politician, lawyer, and businessman who served as the 38th President of El Salvador from 1994 to 1999 as a member of the Nationalist Republican Alliance. He also served as Mayor of San Salvador, the country's capital city, from 1988 to 1994.

events.title: 1994 Austrian European Union membership referendum
events.summary: A referendum on European Union membership was held in Austria on 12 June 1994. The question asked was "Shall the National Council's decision of 5 May 1994 on the Constitutional law (Bundesverfassungsgesetz) concerning the Accession of Austria to the European Union be enacted as law?" The result of the vote was 67% in favour, with a turnout of 82%.

events.title: 1994 Luxembourg general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Luxembourg on 12 June 1994, alongside European Parliament elections. The Christian Social People's Party remained the largest party, winning 21 of the 60 seats in the Chamber of Deputies. It continued the coalition government with the Luxembourg Socialist Workers' Party.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Greece.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India – Pakistan (Kashmir)
events.summary: UCDP records an interstate conflict between Government of India and Government of Pakistan over control of Kashmir, starting 1994-06-28. This episode was active in 1 year (1994–1994), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1994-11-28.

events.title: Tomiichi Murayama takes power
events.summary: Tomiichi Murayama was a Japanese politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 1994 to 1996. He was the country's only socialist premier since Tetsu Katayama in 1948, and is best remembered for the Murayama Statement on the 50th anniversary of the end of World War II, in which he officially apologized for Japan's past colonial wars and aggression.

events.title: 20th G7 summit
events.summary: The 20th G7 Summit was held in Naples, Italy, on 8–10 July 1994. The venue for the summit meetings was the former Royal Palace in Naples.

events.title: 1994 Belarusian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Belarus on 23 June 1994, with a second round on 10 July. They were the first national elections held in Belarus since the country seceded from the Soviet Union three years earlier. The result was an overwhelming victory for Alexander Lukashenko, who received 81% of the vote in the second round.

events.title: 1994 Ukrainian presidential election
events.summary: Early presidential elections were held in Ukraine on 26 June 1994, with a second round on 10 July. They were held ahead of schedule following a compromise between President Leonid Kravchuk and the Verkhovna Rada, the Ukrainian parliament. The elections saw Kravchuk defeated by his former Prime Minister Leonid Kuchma.

events.title: European Council meeting (extraordinary)
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council (extraordinary meeting). Council presidency: Germany.

events.title: Gyula Horn takes power
events.summary: Gyula János Horn was a Hungarian politician who was the Prime Minister of Hungary from 1994 to 1998.

events.title: Terrorist attack: AMIA bombing
events.summary: The Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina, a Jewish community center in Buenos Aires, Argentina, was bombed on 18 July 1994. Executed as a suicide attack, a bomb-laden van was driven into the AMIA building and subsequently detonated, killing 85 people and injuring over 300. To date, the bombing remains the deadliest terrorist attack in Argentine history.

events.title: Leonid Kuchma takes power
events.summary: Leonid Danylovych Kuchma is a Ukrainian politician who served as the second president of Ukraine from 19 July 1994 to 23 January 2005.

events.title: Alexander Lukashenko takes power
events.summary: Alexander Grigoryevich Lukashenko is a Belarusian politician who has been the first and only president of Belarus since the office's establishment in 1994, making him the current longest-tenured European president.

events.title: 1994 Labour Party leadership election
events.summary: The 1994 Labour Party leadership election was held on 21 July 1994 following the death of the incumbent leader, John Smith, on 12 May. Tony Blair won the leadership and became Prime Minister after winning the 1997 general election.

events.title: Coup: 1994 Gambian coup d'état
events.summary: In the 1994 Gambian coup d'état, a group of soldiers led by 29-year-old Lieutenant Yahya Jammeh seized power in a coup d'état on the morning of 22 July, ousting Dawda Jawara, who had been President of The Gambia since it became a Republic in 1970.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs NDFB (Bodoland)
