events.title: Bertie Ahern takes power
events.summary: Bartholomew Patrick "Bertie" Ahern is an Irish former Fianna Fáil politician who served as Taoiseach from 1997 to 2008, and as Leader of Fianna Fáil from 1994 to 2008. A Teachta Dála (TD) from 1977 to 2011, he served as Leader of the Opposition from 1994 to 1997.

events.title: 1997 Albanian monarchy referendum
events.summary: A referendum on restoring the monarchy was held in Albania on 29 June 1997 alongside parliamentary elections. The proposal was rejected by 66.7% of voters. However, former Crown Prince Leka claimed that 65.7% voted in favour.

events.title: 1997 Albanian parliamentary election
events.summary: Early parliamentary elections were held in Albania on 29 June 1997 alongside a simultaneous referendum on restoring the monarchy, with a second round of voting for 32 seats on 6 July. The elections were called as a response to the 1997 Albanian civil unrest.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Eritrea vs EIJM - AS
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Eritrea and EIJM - AS over control of the government, starting 1997-06-30. This episode was active in 1 year (1997–1997), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1997-06-30.

events.title: Mesut Yılmaz takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: Ahmet Mesut Yılmaz was a Turkish politician. He was the leader of the Motherland Party from 1991 to 2002, and served three times as Prime Minister of Turkey. His first two prime-ministerial terms lasted just months, while the third ran from June 1997 to January 1999.

events.title: Hong Kong handed over to China
events.summary: The handover of Hong Kong from the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to the People's Republic of China occurred at midnight on 1 July 1997. This event ended 156 years of British rule, dating back to the capture of Hong Kong Island in 1841 during the First Opium War.

events.title: 1997 Mexican legislative election
events.summary: Legislative elections were held in Mexico on 6 July 1997. The Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) won 239 of the 500 seats in the Chamber of Deputies, the first time it had failed to win a majority.

events.title: 1997 Madrid NATO summit
events.summary: The 1997 Madrid summit was a meeting of the heads of state and heads of government of the sixteen members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and their partner countries held in Madrid, Spain, on 8–9 July 1997. It was the 15th NATO summit and the second in 1997, the previous one being held in Paris.

events.title: Fatos Nano takes power
events.summary: Fatos Thanas Nano was an Albanian socialist politician who served as Prime Minister of Albania in 1991, from 1997 to 1998 and from 2002 to 2005.

events.title: Guntars Krasts takes power
events.summary: Guntars Krasts is a Latvian politician, former Prime Minister, and former Member of the European Parliament for the single Latvia constituency. Born in Riga, he was the Minister of Economy of Latvia from December 1995 to August 1997, Prime Minister of Latvia from August 1997 to November 1998, and the Deputy Prime Minister from November 1998 to June 1999.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Comoros vs MPA/Republic of Anjouan (Anjouan)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Comoros and MPA/Republic of Anjouan over control of Anjouan, starting 1997-09-05. This episode was active in 1 year (1997–1997), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1997-09-05.

events.title: 1997 Scottish devolution referendum
events.summary: The Scottish devolution referendum of 1997 was a pre-legislative referendum held in Scotland on 11 September 1997 over whether there was support for the creation of a Scottish Parliament with devolved powers, and whether the Parliament should have tax-varying powers.

events.title: 1997 Norwegian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Norway on 14 and 15 September 1997. Prior to the election Prime Minister Thorbjørn Jagland of the Labour Party had issued the 36.9 ultimatum declaring that the government would step down unless it gained 36.9% of the vote, the percentage gained by the Labour Party in 1993 under Gro Harlem Brundtland.

events.title: 1997 Welsh devolution referendum
events.summary: The 1997 Welsh devolution referendum was a pre-legislative referendum held in Wales on 18 September 1997 over whether there was support for the creation of a National Assembly for Wales, and therefore a degree of self-government.

events.title: 1997 Polish parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Poland on 21 September 1997. All 460 members of the Sejm and 100 senators of the Senate were elected. The liberal conservative party Solidarity Electoral Action won the most seats in both chambers of parliament and formed a coalition government with the Freedom Union, another liberal party.

events.title: 1997 Serbian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in the Yugoslav province of Serbia on 21 September 1997, to elect the president and members of the National Assembly. With no presidential candidate receiving over 50% of the vote in the first round, a second round was held on 5 October.

events.title: Treaty signed: Treaty of Amsterdam
events.summary: The Treaty of Amsterdam, officially the Treaty of Amsterdam amending the Treaty on European Union, the Treaties establishing the European Communities and certain related acts, was signed on 2 October 1997, and entered into force on 1 May 1999; it made substantial changes to the Maastricht Treaty, which had been signed in 1992.

events.title: 1997 Botswana electoral reform referendum
events.summary: A referendum on electoral reform was held in Botswana on 4 October 1997. The referendum had three separate proposals, and came following promises made by President Quett Masire after violent protests in 1995. All three proposals were passed, although voter turnout was only around 17%.

events.title: Kjell Magne Bondevik takes power
events.summary: Kjell Magne Bondevik is a Norwegian Lutheran minister and politician. As leader of the Christian Democratic Party, he served as the prime minister of Norway from 1997 to 2000, and from 2001 to 2005, making him, after Erna Solberg, Norway's second longest serving non-Labour Party prime minister since World War II.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Niger vs UFRA
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Niger and UFRA over control of the government, starting 1997-10-19. This episode was active in 1 year (1997–1997), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1997-11-28.

events.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 1997
events.summary: The 1997 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting was the 15th Meeting of the Heads of Government of the Commonwealth of Nations. It was held in Edinburgh, Scotland, between 24 October and 27 October 1997, and hosted by Prime Minister Tony Blair.

events.title: 1997 Anjouan independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held on Anjouan, an island in the Comoros, on 26 October 1997. Over 99% of voters voted in favour of independence. However, the vote was not recognised and the island returned to the control of the Comorian government in 2001.

events.title: 1997 San Marino referendum
events.summary: A referendum was held in San Marino on 26 October 1997. Voters were asked whether they approved of a proposal that any corporation buying, administering or selling land and property would have to be a public company. It was approved by 88.1% of voters.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Chad vs FARF, MDD
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Chad and FARF, MDD over control of the government, starting 1997-10-30. This episode was active in 7 years (1997–2003), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 2003-12-14.

events.title: Seventeenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
events.summary: The Seventeenth Amendment of the Constitution Act 1997 amended the Constitution of Ireland to provide that the confidentiality of meetings of the cabinet would not prevent the High Court from ordering that certain information be disclosed when this was in the public interest.

events.title: 1997 Irish presidential election
events.summary: The 1997 Irish presidential election was held on Thursday, 30 October 1997. It was the eleventh presidential election to be held in Ireland, and only the sixth to be contested by more than one candidate.

events.title: 1997 Hungarian NATO membership referendum
events.summary: A referendum on joining NATO was held in Hungary on 16 November 1997. The proposal was approved by 85% of voters, with a voter turnout of 49%.

events.title: Terrorist attack: Luxor massacre
events.summary: The Luxor massacre was a terrorist attack that occurred on 17 November 1997 in Egypt. It was perpetrated by al-Jama'a al-Islamiyya and resulted in the deaths of 62 people, most of whom were tourists. It took place at Dayr al-Bahri, an archaeological site located across the Nile from the city of Luxor.

events.title: European Council meeting (extraordinary)
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council (extraordinary meeting). Council presidency: Luxembourg.

events.title: Brest Congress
events.summary: The Brest Congress was the eighteenth national congress of the French Socialist Party. It took place from November 21 to 23, 1997.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Philippines vs CPP
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Philippines and CPP over control of the government, starting 1997-11-23. This episode was active in 1 year (1997–1997), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1997-12-30.

events.title: APEC Canada 1997
events.summary: APEC Canada 1997 was a series of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings focused on economic cooperation, held in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada on 24–25 November 1997. It was the fifth APEC meeting in history, and the second held in the Americas.

events.title: 1997 Honduran general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Honduras to elect a president and parliament on 30 November 1997. They were also the first elections in which the left wing Democratic Unification Party was allowed to stand. Closed list PR was used to elect Congress.

events.title: 1997 United Nations Climate Change Conference
events.summary: The United Nations Climate Change Conferences are yearly conferences held in the framework of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

events.title: Treaty signed: Ottawa Treaty
events.summary: The Convention on the Prohibition of the Use, Stockpiling, Production and Transfer of Anti-Personnel Mines and on their Destruction of 1997, known informally as the Ottawa Treaty, the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention, or often simply the Mine Ban Treaty, aims at eliminating anti-personnel landmines (APLs) around the world.

events.title: 1997 Serbian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in the Yugoslav province of Serbia on 7 December 1997, following the annulment of the results of the September–October elections due to low voter turnout. As no candidate won over 50% of the popular vote in the first round, a runoff was scheduled for 21 December.

events.title: Treaty signed: Kyoto Protocol
events.summary: The Kyoto Protocol (Japanese: 京都議定書, Hepburn: Kyōto Giteisho) was an international treaty which extended the 1992 United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) that commits state parties to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, based on the scientific consensus that global warming is occurring and that human-made CO2 emissions are driving it.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Luxembourg.

events.title: Josef Tošovský takes power
events.summary: Josef Tošovský is a Czech economist and former governor of Czech National Bank. From 17 December 1997 to 17 July 1998 he was the prime minister of the Czech Republic in a caretaker government.

events.title: 1997 Jamaican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Jamaica on 18 December 1997. The ruling People's National Party of Prime Minister P. J. Patterson won 50 of the 60 seats defeating the main opposition Jamaica Labour Party.

events.title: 1997 Slovenian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Slovenia on 23 November 1997. The result was a victory for incumbent Milan Kučan, who won 55.54% of the vote. Voter turnout was 68.65%.

events.title: Flavio Cotti takes power
events.summary: Flavio Cotti was a Swiss politician who served as member of the Federal Council from 1986 to 1999. He was a member of the Christian Democratic People's Party from the canton of Ticino. In the 1990s, Cotti led the Swiss government's unsuccessful attempts to further Switzerland's political integration into the European Union.

events.title: 1997–98 Lithuanian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Lithuania in December 1997 and January 1998. Artūras Paulauskas finished first in the first round on 21 December 1997 with a significant margin, with Valdas Adamkus finishing second, but neither received a majority of the vote. Adamkus defeated Paulauskas in the runoff, held on 4 January 1998.

events.title: 1998 Cuban parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Cuba on 11 January 1998 alongside elections to the fourteen Provincial Assemblies. A list of 601 candidates for the 601 seats was provided by the National Candidature Commission. Voter turnout was reported to be 98.35%.

events.title: 1998 Czech presidential election
events.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in the Czech Republic on 20 January 1998 to elect a new president. The Parliament re-elected incumbent President Václav Havel in the second round. The arrest of an opposition candidate, Miroslav Sládek, was criticised by Havel's opponents.

events.title: 1998 Costa Rican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Costa Rica on 1 February 1998. Miguel Ángel Rodríguez of the Social Christian Unity Party won the presidential election, whilst his party also won the parliamentary election. Voter turnout was 70%, the lowest since the 1950s.

events.title: 1998 Monegasque general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Monaco on 1 February 1998, with a second round of voting on 8 February. The result was a victory for the National and Democratic Union, which won all 18 seats in the National Council.

events.title: Robert Kocharyan takes power
events.summary: Robert Sedraki Kocharyan is an Armenian politician. He served as the President of the Nagorno-Karabakh Republic from 1994 to 1997 and Prime Minister of Nagorno-Karabakh from 1992 to 1994. He served as the second President of Armenia between 1998 and 2008 and as Prime Minister of Armenia from 1997 to 1998.

events.title: 1998 Cypriot presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Cyprus on 8 February 1998, with a second round on 15 February. The result was a victory for Glafcos Clerides of the Democratic Rally after he finished as runner-up behind Georgios Iacovou in the first round. Voter turnout was 92% in the first round and 93% in the second.

events.title: Valdas Adamkus takes power
events.summary: Valdas Adamkus is a Lithuanian politician, diplomat and civil engineer and an American civil servant. He served as the fifth and seventh president of Lithuania from 1998 to 2003 and again from 2004 to 2009.

events.title: 1998 Israeli presidential election
events.summary: An election for President of Israel was held in the Knesset on 4 March 1998.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Yugoslavia vs UCK (Kosovo)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Serbia (Yugoslavia) and UCK over control of Kosovo, starting 1998-03-06. This episode was active in 2 years (1998–1999), 2 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1999-11-21.

events.title: 1998 Danish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Denmark on 11 March 1998. Although the centre-right parties led by Venstre had been expected to win, the Social Democratic Party-led government of Poul Nyrup Rasmussen remained in power in a very close vote that required several recounts.

events.title: 1998 Armenian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Armenia on 16 March 1998, with a second round on 30 March. The result was a victory for independent candidate Robert Kocharyan, who won 58.9% of the vote in the second round. Turnout was 63.5% in the first round and 68.1% in the second.

events.title: 1998 Moldovan parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Moldova on 22 March 1998. The Party of Communists of the Republic of Moldova (PCRM) emerged as the largest party in Parliament, winning 40 of the 101 seats.

events.title: 1998 Ukrainian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Ukraine on 29 March 1998. The Communist Party of Ukraine remained the largest party in the Verkhovna Rada, winning 121 of the 445 seats, but no party gained a majority of seats, resulting in a hung parliament that eventually resulted in elements of the left supportive of president Leonid Kuchma being placed in leadership…

events.title: Gavril Dejeu takes power
events.summary: Gavril Dejeu is a Romanian politician who served as Minister of Interior in Victor Ciorbea's cabinet. He was also acting Prime Minister of Romania from 30 March to 17 April 1998.

events.title: Treaty signed: Good Friday Agreement
events.summary: The Good Friday Agreement or Belfast Agreement is a pair of agreements signed on 10 April 1998 that ended most of the violence of the Troubles, an ethnic and national conflict in Northern Ireland since the late 1960s. It was a major development in the Northern Ireland peace process of the 1990s.

events.title: Radu Vasile takes power
events.summary: Radu Vasile was a Romanian politician, historian, academic, writer and poet who served as Prime Minister of Romania from 17 April 1998 to 13 December 1999. A leading member of the Christian Democratic National Peasants' Party (PNȚ-CD), he played a prominent role within the Romanian Democratic Convention (CDR).

events.title: 1998 Austrian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Austria on 19 April 1998. The result was a victory for the incumbent, President Thomas Klestil, who sought re-election as an independent candidate.

events.title: 1998 Serbian foreign mediation in Kosovo referendum
events.summary: A referendum on foreign mediation in Kosovo was held in the Republic of Serbia on 23 April 1998. Voters were asked "Do you approve the participation of foreign representatives in solving the problems in Kosovo and Metohija?" The proposal was rejected by 96.53% of voters. The referendum was boycotted by Kosovan Albanians.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Angola vs UNITA
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Angola and UNITA over control of the government, starting 1998-05-02. This episode was active in 5 years (1998–2002), 4 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 2002-04-01.

events.title: European Council meeting (extraordinary)
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council (extraordinary meeting). Council presidency: United Kingdom.

events.title: May 1998 Indonesia riots
events.summary: The May 1998 Indonesia riots, also known colloquially as the 1998 tragedy or simply the 98 event, were incidents of riots and civil unrest in Indonesia, many of which targeted the country's ethnic Chinese population. The events were mainly in the cities of Jakarta, Medan, Surakarta, Palembang, and Surabaya with smaller incidents in other parts of Indonesia.

events.title: 1998 Dutch general election
events.summary: General elections were held in the Netherlands on 6 May 1998. The elections saw the purple coalition of social democrats and liberals strengthen its majority.

events.title: 1998 Greater London Authority referendum
events.summary: The 1998 Greater London Authority referendum was held in Greater London on 7 May 1998. The referendum asked whether there was support for creating a Greater London Authority composed of a directly elected Mayor of London and a London Assembly to scrutinise the Mayor's actions. Voter turnout was low, at just 34.1%.

events.title: Miguel Ángel Rodríguez Echeverría takes power
events.summary: Miguel Ángel Rodríguez Echeverría is a Costa Rican economist, lawyer, businessman and politician who served as the 43rd President of Costa Rica from 1998 to 2002. A liberal member of the Social Christian Unity Party, he has remained active as a writer and columnist since leaving public office.

events.title: 1998 Hungarian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Hungary on 10 May 1998, with a second round of voting in 175 of the 176 single member constituencies on 24 May.

events.title: 24th G8 summit
events.summary: The 24th G8 Summit was held in Birmingham, England, United Kingdom on 15–17 May 1998. The venue for this summit meeting was the International Convention Centre.

events.title: 1998 Dominican Republic parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Dominican Republic on 16 May 1998. The result was a victory for the opposition Dominican Revolutionary Party-led alliance, which won 83 of the 149 seats in the House of Representatives. Voter turnout was 52.9%.

events.title: Nineteenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
events.summary: The Nineteenth Amendment of the Constitution is an amendment of the Constitution of Ireland which permitted the state to be bound by the British–Irish Agreement and enabled the establishment of shared political institutions between Ireland and Northern Ireland.

events.title: Eighteenth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
events.summary: The Eighteenth Amendment of the Constitution Act 1998 is an amendment of the Constitution of Ireland which permitted the state to ratify the Treaty of Amsterdam. It was approved by referendum on 22 May 1998 and signed into law on the 3 June of the same year.

events.title: 1998 Northern Ireland Good Friday Agreement referendum
events.summary: A referendum was held in Northern Ireland on 22 May 1998 over whether there was support for the Good Friday Agreement. The result was a majority (71.1%) in favour. A simultaneous referendum held in the Republic of Ireland produced an even larger majority (94.4%) in favour.

events.title: 1998 Danish Amsterdam Treaty referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the Amsterdam Treaty was held in Denmark on 28 May 1998. It was approved by 55.1% of voters with a turnout of 76.2%. The treaty subsequently came into effect on 1 May 1999.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Eritrea – Ethiopia (Common border)
events.summary: UCDP records an interstate conflict between Government of Eritrea and Government of Ethiopia over control of Common border, starting 1998-05-31. This episode was active in 3 years (1998–2000), 3 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 2000-06-18.

events.title: 1998 San Marino general election
events.summary: General elections were held in San Marino on 31 May 1998. The Sammarinese Christian Democratic Party remained the largest party, winning 25 of the 60 seats in the Grand and General Council, and continued their coalition with the Sammarinese Socialist Party.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Guinea-Bissau vs Military Junta for the Consolidation of Democracy, Peace and Justice
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Guinea-Bissau (backed by Government of Guinea, Government of Senegal) and Military Junta for the Consolidation of Democracy, Peace and Justice over control of the government, starting 1998-06-07. This episode was active in 2 years (1998–1999), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1999-05-07.

events.title: 1998 Portuguese abortion referendum
events.summary: On 28 June 1998 a referendum on a new abortion law was conducted in Portugal; it was the second national referendum in the Portuguese history and the first after the 1974 Carnation Revolution.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: United Kingdom.

events.title: 1998 Vincentian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines on 15 June 1998. Although the Unity Labour Party (ULP) received a majority of the public vote, the New Democratic Party (NDP) won a majority of seats, the first time the party receiving a majority of the vote had failed to win the elections since 1966. Voter turnout was 67%.

events.title: 1998 Czech parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Czech Republic on 19 and 20 June 1998. The Czech Social Democratic Party emerged as the largest party, winning 74 of the 200 seats. Voter turnout was 73.9%.

events.title: Treaty signed: Aarhus Convention
events.summary: The UNECE Convention on Access to Information, Public Participation in Decision-making and Access to Justice in Environmental Matters, usually known as the Aarhus Convention, was signed on 25 June 1998 in the Danish city of Aarhus. It entered into force on 30 October 2001. In April 2023, it had 49 parties—48 states and the European Union.

events.title: Viktor Orbán takes power
events.summary: Viktor Mihály Orbán is a Hungarian lawyer and politician who served as the prime minister of Hungary from 1998 to 2002 and from 2010 to 2026. He has also been the president of Fidesz, which has been variously characterised as a Christian nationalist, illiberal, and far-right political party.

events.title: Miloš Zeman takes power
events.summary: Miloš Zeman is a Czech politician who served as the third president of the Czech Republic from 2013 to 2023. He also previously served as the prime minister of the Czech Republic from 1998 to 2002. As leader of the Czech Social Democratic Party from 1993 to 2001, he is credited with the revival of the party into one of the country's major political forces.

events.title: Treaty signed: Rome Statute
events.summary: The Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court is the treaty that established the International Criminal Court (ICC). It was adopted at a diplomatic conference in Rome, Italy on 17 July 1998 and entered into force on 1 July 2002. As of January 2025, 125 states are party to the statute.

events.title: Keizō Obuchi takes power
events.summary: Keizō Obuchi was a Japanese politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan and President of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) from 1998 to 2000.

events.title: 1998 Nevis independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in Nevis on 10 August 1998. Although it was approved by 62% of voters, a two-thirds majority was necessary for the referendum to succeed. If it had passed, Nevis would have seceded from the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: United Kingdom vs RIRA (Northern Ireland)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of United Kingdom and RIRA over control of Northern Ireland, starting 1998-08-15. This episode was active in 1 year (1998–1998), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1998-08-15.

events.title: Terrorist attack: Omagh bombing
events.summary: A car bombing took place in the town of Omagh in County Tyrone, Northern Ireland on 15 August 1998. It was carried out by the Real Irish Republican Army, a Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) splinter group who opposed the IRA's ceasefire and the Good Friday Agreement, signed earlier in the year.

events.title: 1998 Belizean general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Belize on 27 August 1998. The result was a victory for the People's United Party, which won 26 of the 29 seats and Said Musa was elected as prime minister for the first time. Voter turnout was 90%, the highest since independence.

events.title: Said Musa takes power
events.summary: Said Wilbert Musa is a Belizean lawyer and politician. He was the third prime minister of Belize from 28 August 1998 to 8 February 2008.

events.title: 1998 Mexican Fobaproa funds referendum
events.summary: An unofficial referendum on use of Fobaproa funds was held in Mexico on 30 August 1998. It was organised by the opposition Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), who proposed that only small- and medium-sized businesses would be compensated by the funds.

events.title: Erik Lahnstein takes power
events.summary: Erik Lahnstein is a Norwegian politician for the Centre Party.

events.title: 1998 Panamanian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Panama on 30 August 1998. Voters were asked whether they approved of amending the 1972 constitution to allow the President and Vice President to be re-elected for a second term and dismissal of MPs by their own parties. Only 34.3% voted in favour of the reforms, with a turnout of 65.4%.

events.title: 1998 Maltese general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Malta on 5 September 1998. The result was a victory for the Nationalist Party, which won 35 of the 65 seats.

events.title: Eddie Fenech Adami takes power
events.summary: Edoardo "Eddie" Fenech Adami is a Maltese politician and lawyer who served as the prime minister of Malta from 1987 until 1996, and again from 1998 until 2004. Subsequently, he was the seventh president of Malta from 2004 to 2009.

events.title: Treaty signed: Rotterdam Convention
events.summary: The Rotterdam Convention is a multilateral treaty to promote shared responsibilities in relation to importation of hazardous chemicals. The convention promotes open exchange of information and calls on exporters of hazardous chemicals to use proper labeling, include directions on safe handling, and inform purchasers of any known restrictions or bans.

events.title: 1998 Bosnian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Bosnia and Herzegovina on 12 and 13 September 1998. Voter turnout was 67.99% in the parliamentary election and 67.87% in the presidential election.

events.title: 1998 Swedish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Sweden on 20 September 1998. The Swedish Social Democratic Party remained the largest party in the Riksdag, winning 131 of the 349 seats.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Lesotho vs Military faction (Lesotho)
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Lesotho (backed by Government of Botswana, Government of South Africa) and Military faction (Lesotho) over control of the government, starting 1998-09-22. This episode was active in 1 year (1998–1998), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1998-09-28.

events.title: Kjell Magne Bondevik takes power
events.summary: Kjell Magne Bondevik is a Norwegian Lutheran minister and politician. As leader of the Christian Democratic Party, he served as the prime minister of Norway from 1997 to 2000, and from 2001 to 2005, making him, after Erna Solberg, Norway's second longest serving non-Labour Party prime minister since World War II.

events.title: 1998 Slovak privatisation referendum
events.summary: A referendum on banning the privatisation of strategically important state-owned companies was held in Slovakia on 25 and 26 September 1998. Although approved by 84.3% of those voting, voter turnout was just 44.1% and the referendum was declared invalid due to insufficient turnout.

events.title: 1998 Slovak parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Slovakia on 25 and 26 September 1998. The elections resulted in the defeat of the Vladimír Mečiar government and the election of Mikuláš Dzurinda as Prime Minister.

events.title: 1998 German federal election
events.summary: A federal election was held in Germany on 27 September 1998 to elect the members of the 14th Bundestag. The Social Democratic Party (SPD) emerged as the largest faction in parliament for the first time since 1972, with its leader Gerhard Schröder becoming chancellor. The Christian Democrats had their worst election result since 1949.

events.title: Pandeli Majko takes power
events.summary: Pandeli Sotir Majko is an Albanian socialist politician. He served twice as Prime Minister of Albania; once from 1998 to 1999, and again in 2002.

events.title: 1998 Northern Territory referendum
events.summary: A referendum was held in the Northern Territory on Saturday, 3 October 1998, to decide whether the Territory should become a State of the Commonwealth of Australia. The Country Liberal Party government, and its federal counterpart, supported the Yes case.

events.title: 1998 Latvian citizenship referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the citizenship law was held in Latvia on 3 October 1998. The Saeima had made amendments to the law in June that increased the opportunities for naturalisation and provided the additional option of obtaining Latvian citizenship for non-citizens (nepilsoņi) and stateless persons (bezvalstnieki) born in Latvia from August 1991 onwards.

events.title: 1998 Latvian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Latvia on 3 October 1998. The People's Party emerged as the largest party in the Saeima, winning 24 of the 100 seats.

events.title: 1998 Azerbaijani presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Azerbaijan on 11 October 1998. The result was a victory for Heydar Aliyev of the New Azerbaijan Party, who received 78% of the vote. Voter turnout was reported to be 79%.

events.title: Živko Radišić takes power
events.summary: Živko Radišić was a Bosnian Serb politician who served as the Serb member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1998 to 2002. He previously served as mayor of Banja Luka from 1977 to 1982. Radišić was a founding member and president of the Socialist Party from 1996 to 2002.

events.title: 1998 Kyrgyz constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Kyrgyzstan on 17 October 1998. The main provisions of the referendum were the introduction of the private ownership of land for citizens of Kyrgyzstan; a change in the distribution of seats in parliament - increasing number of seats in Legislative Assembly from 35 to 60 and reducing the number of seats in Assembly of…

events.title: 1998 Macedonian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Macedonia on 18 October 1998, with a second round on 1 November. VMRO-DPMNE emerged as the largest party, winning 49 of the 120 seats, and later formed a coalition government with Democratic Alternative and the Democratic Party of Albanians.

events.title: Massimo D'Alema takes power
events.summary: Massimo D'Alema is an Italian politician and journalist who was the 53rd prime minister of Italy from 1998 to 2000. He was Deputy Prime Minister of Italy and Italian Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2006 to 2008. D'Alema also served for a time as national secretary of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS).

events.title: Natural disaster: Hurricane Mitch
events.summary: Hurricane Mitch was an extremely powerful, deadly and catastrophic tropical cyclone in 1998 that caused 11,374 fatalities in Central America, becoming the second-deadliest Atlantic hurricane on record. It was the deadliest hurricane in Central American history, surpassing Hurricane Fifi, which killed slightly fewer people in the same area in 1974.

events.title: Treaty signed: Wye River Memorandum
events.summary: The Wye River Memorandum was an agreement negotiated between Israel and the Palestinian Authority at a summit in Wye River, Maryland, U.S., held 15–23 October 1998. The Memorandum aimed to resume the implementation of the 1995 Interim Agreement on the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.

events.title: European Council meeting (informal)
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council (informal meeting). Council presidency: Austria.

events.title: Gerhard Schröder takes power
events.summary: Gerhard "Gerd" Fritz Kurt Schröder is a German former politician and lobbyist who served as Chancellor of Germany from 1998 to 2005. From 1999 to 2004, he was also the Leader of the Social Democratic Party of Germany (SPD). As chancellor, he led a coalition government of the SPD and Alliance 90/The Greens.

events.title: Mikuláš Dzurinda takes power
events.summary: Mikuláš Dzurinda is a Slovak politician who was the prime minister of Slovakia from 30 October 1998 to 4 July 2006. Dzurinda is the founder and leader of the Slovak Democratic Coalition (SDK) and then the Slovak Democratic and Christian Union (SDKÚ–DS).

events.title: 1998 United Nations Climate Change Conference
events.summary: The 1998 United Nations Climate Change Conference took place in November 1998 in Buenos Aires, Argentina. The conference included the 4th Conference of the Parties (COP4) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). It had been expected that the remaining issues unresolved in Kyoto would be finalized at this meeting.

events.title: 1998 New Caledonian Nouméa Accord referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the Nouméa Accord was held in New Caledonia on 8 November 1998. It was approved by 71.85% of voters. The proportion of voters in favour was highest in the Loyalty Islands and lowest in the South Province.

events.title: 1998 Portuguese regionalisation referendum
events.summary: A referendum on creating administrative regions was held in Portugal on 8 November 1998. Two questions were put to voters, the first on implementing the regions, and the second specifically asked whether voters approved of the new region for their area. Both proposals were rejected by wide margins by voters.

events.title: 1998 Albanian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Albania on 22 November 1998. Voters were asked whether they approved of the constitution. It was approved by 93.5% of voters with a turnout of 50.6%, and came into force on 28 November.

events.title: Vilis Krištopans takes power
events.summary: Vilis Krištopans is a Latvian politician who served as the prime minister of Latvia from 26 November 1998 to 15 July 1999.

events.title: Ljubčo Georgievski takes power
events.summary: Ljubčo Georgievski is a Macedonian politician and writer who served as the only Vice President of Macedonia from January to October 1991 and as the Prime Minister of Macedonia from 1998 to 2002. He advocated for the country's independence.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Austria.

events.title: 1998 Puerto Rican status referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the political status of Puerto Rico was held on December 13, 1998, five years after an inconclusive result in a 1993 status referendum.

events.title: 1998 Slovak presidential election
events.summary: The 1998 Slovak Presidential elections were held from 20 January to 17 December 1998. The Slovak parliament failed to elect the new president of Slovakia which led to the introduction of a direct election in 1999. A candidate would have needed to receive 90 votes to be elected.

events.title: Impeachment of Bill Clinton
events.summary: Bill Clinton, the 42nd president of the United States, was impeached by the United States House of Representatives of the 105th United States Congress on December 19, 1998. The House adopted two articles of impeachment against Clinton, with the specific charges against Clinton being lying under oath and obstruction of justice.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ethiopia vs ONLF (Ogaden)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Ethiopia and ONLF over control of Ogaden, starting 1998-12-31. This episode was active in 19 years (1998–2016), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2016-12-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ethiopia vs OLF (Oromiya)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Ethiopia and OLF over control of Oromiya, starting 1998-12-31. This episode was active in 16 years (1998–2013), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2013-12-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs PLA (Manipur)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and PLA over control of Manipur, starting 1998-12-31. This episode was active in 3 years (1998–2000), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2000-12-20.

events.title: Euro introduced in eleven EU countries
events.summary: The euro is the official currency of 21 of the 27 member states of the European Union. This group of states is officially known as the euro area, more commonly named the eurozone. Each euro is subdivided into 100 cents.

events.title: Ruth Dreifuss takes power
events.summary: Ruth Dreifuss is a Swiss economist, unionist and politician who served as a member of the Federal Council from 1993 to 2002. She served as Vice President of Switzerland in 1998 and as President of Switzerland in 1999 for the Social Democratic Party.

events.title: 1999 Slovenian coal power station referendum
events.summary: A referendum on building a coal-fired power plant was held in Slovenia on 10 January 1999. Voters were asked whether they approved of the construction of the TET3 coal-fired power plant. The proposal was rejected by 79.8% of voters, although voter turnout was just 27.3%.

events.title: Bülent Ecevit takes power
events.summary: Mustafa Bülent Ecevit was a Turkish statesman, poet, writer, scholar, and journalist. He served as the Prime Minister of Turkey four times between 1974 and 2002, specifically in 1974, 1977, 1978–79, and 1999–2002. Ecevit was Chairman of the Republican People's Party (CHP) from 1972 to 1980, and became Chairman of the Democratic Left Party (DSP) in 1987.

events.title: 1999 Grenadian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Grenada on 18 January 1999. The governing New National Party of Prime Minister Keith Mitchell was re-elected after winning all 15 seats. Voter turnout was 56.5%.

events.title: 1999 Barbadian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Barbados on 20 January 1999. The result was a landslide victory for the Barbados Labour Party led by Owen Arthur, which won 26 of the 28 seats. The opposition Democratic Labour Party led by David Thompson, only won two seats. Voter turnout was 63.4%.

events.title: 1999 Liechtenstein health insurance referendum
events.summary: A referendum on health insurance was held in Liechtenstein on 31 January 1999. The proposal, regarding modification of health insurance reimbursements, was rejected by 66% of voters.

events.title: European Council meeting (informal)
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council (informal meeting). Council presidency: Germany.

events.title: 1999 Salvadoran presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in El Salvador on 7 March 1999. The result was a victory for Francisco Flores of the Nationalist Republican Alliance, who won in the first round with 51.96% of the vote.

events.title: 1999 Estonian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Estonia on 7 March 1999. The newly elected 101 members of the 9th Riigikogu assembled at Toompea Castle in Tallinn within ten days of the election. The elections proved disastrous for the ruling Estonian Coalition Party, which won only seven seats together with two of its smaller allies.

events.title: 1999 Antiguan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Antigua and Barbuda on 9 March 1999. The elections were won by the governing Antigua Labour Party. Lester Bird was re-elected Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda. Voter turnout was 63.6%.

events.title: 1999 Finnish parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Finland on 21 March 1999. Despite suffering significant losses, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) remained the largest party of the Eduskunta and Paavo Lipponen remained Prime Minister.

events.title: 1999 Mexican referendums
events.summary: A series of unofficial referendums on native rights and good governance was held in Mexico on 21 March 1999. It was organised by the Zapatista Army of National Liberation (EZLN), who proposed the government function in the interests of the people, that the country demilitarize in order to promote peace, that indigenous Mexicans be fully included in national…

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Germany.

events.title: Mart Laar takes power
events.summary: Mart Laar is an Estonian politician and historian. He served as the Prime Minister of Estonia from 1992 to 1994 and from 1999 to 2002. Laar is credited with having helped bring about Estonia's rapid economic development during the 1990s. He is a member of the centre-right Isamaa party.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Uzbekistan vs IMU
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Uzbekistan and IMU over control of the government, starting 1999-03-30. This episode was active in 2 years (1999–2000), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2000-10-01.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Eritrea vs EIJM - AS
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Eritrea and EIJM - AS over control of the government, starting 1999-04-04. This episode was active in 1 year (1999–1999), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1999-11-29.

events.title: Battle of Košare
events.summary: The Battle of Košare was fought during the Kosovo War between the forces of FR Yugoslavia and the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), the latter supported by the NATO air forces and Albanian Army. The battle was fought around Košare on the border between FR Yugoslavia and Albania from 9 April 1999 until 10 June 1999 during the NATO bombing of FR Yugoslavia.

events.title: Coup: 1999 Nigerien coup d'état
events.summary: The 1999 Nigerien coup d'état occurred on 9 April 1999 and resulted in the death of President Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara and the installation of Daouda Malam Wanké as President on 11 April.

events.title: Assassination of Ali Sayyad Shirazi
events.summary: On 10 April 1999, 6:45 a.m local time, Ali Sayyad Shirazi, the deputy chief of staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, was assassinated while leaving his home for work. He was killed by an Mojahedin-e Khalq (MEK) assailant, an Iranian opposition group, who was disguised as a street cleaner and handed Shirazi a letter just before shooting him.

events.title: European Council meeting (informal)
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council (informal meeting). Council presidency: Germany.

events.title: 1999 Italian referendum
events.summary: An abrogative referendum on the electoral law was held in Italy on 18 April 1999. Voters were asked whether they approved of replacing the mixed-member proportional representation electoral system with one based solely on single-member constituencies, with the 25% of seats instead allocated to the second-placed in the constituencies with the most votes.

events.title: 1999 Turkish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Turkey on Sunday, 18 April 1999. For the first time, local, council and parliamentary elections were held on the same day.

events.title: 1999 Washington NATO summit
events.summary: The 1999 Washington summit was the 16th NATO summit, a three-day meeting held in Washington, D.C., on April 23–25, 1999.

events.title: April 1999 Venezuelan constitutional referendum
events.summary: A referendum on convening a Constituent Assembly was held in Venezuela on 25 April 1999. It was promoted by President Hugo Chávez, with voters asked two questions on convening a National Constituent Assembly and how that body should be elected. Both proposals were approved by over 80% of voters.

events.title: 1999 Panamanian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Panama on 2 May 1999, electing both a new President of the Republic and a new Legislative Assembly.

events.title: 1999 National Assembly for Wales election
events.summary: The inaugural election for the National Assembly for Wales was held on Thursday 6 May 1999 to elect 60 members to the National Assembly for Wales. It was the first devolved general election held in Wales after the successful 1997 Welsh devolution referendum. The election was held alongside the Scottish Parliament election and English local elections.

events.title: 1999 Icelandic parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Iceland on 8 May 1999. The Independence Party remained the largest party in the Althing, winning 26 of the 63 seats. The coalition government of the Independence Party and Progressive Party remained in office, with Davíð Oddsson continuing as Prime Minister.

events.title: 1999 Italian presidential election
events.summary: The 1999 Italian presidential election was held on 13 May 1999. As a second-level, indirect election, only Members of Parliament and regional deputies were entitled to vote.

events.title: 1999 Slovak presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Slovakia on 15 May 1999, with a second round on 29 May. Following a constitutional amendment in 1998 that introduced direct presidential elections for the first time, they resulted in a victory for Rudolf Schuster, who received 57% of the vote in the run-off.

events.title: 1999 Belarusian presidential election
events.summary: The 1999 Belarusian presidential election was a political protest action by members of Belarusian opposition who did not recognise the 1996 constitutional reform which extended Alexander Lukashenko's presidential term.

events.title: 1999 Guatemalan constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Guatemala on 16 May 1999. It featured four questions; one on defining the nation and social rights one on reforming Congress, one on reforming the executive and one on reforming the judiciary. All four were rejected by voters, although turnout was just 18.6%.

events.title: 1999 Israeli general election
events.summary: Early general elections for both the prime minister and the Knesset were held in Israel on 17 May 1999 following a vote of no confidence in the government; the incumbent Likud Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, ran for re-election.

events.title: 1999 Moldovan constitutional referendum
events.summary: A consultative constitutional referendum was held in Moldova on 23 May 1999. It was initiated by President Petru Lucinschi and asked voters whether they approved of changing the system of government to a presidential system. The proposal was approved by 64% of voters.

events.title: Treaty signed: Montreal Convention
events.summary: The Montreal Convention is a multilateral treaty adopted on 28 May 1999 by member states of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and entered into force on 4 November 2003. It updated and replaced parts of the earlier Warsaw Convention and Hague Protocol, which had governed international air travel since the early 20th century.

events.title: 1999 Armenian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Armenia on 30 May 1999. There were 75 constituency seats and 56 elected on a national basis using proportional representation. The result was a victory for the Unity Bloc, which won 62 of the 131 seats.

events.title: Francisco Flores Pérez takes power
events.summary: Francisco Guillermo Flores Pérez was a Salvadoran politician who served as the 39th President of El Salvador from 1 June 1999 to 1 June 2004 as a member of the conservative Nationalist Republican Alliance (ARENA). He previously served as a deputy of the Legislative Assembly from 1994 to 1999, having been president of the Assembly from 1997 to 1999.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Indonesia vs GAM (Aceh)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Indonesia and GAM over control of Aceh, starting 1999-06-01. This episode was active in 7 years (1999–2005), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2005-10-12.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Germany.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Philippines vs CPP
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Philippines and CPP over control of the government, starting 1999-06-06. This episode was active in 27 years (1999–2025), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year) and was still active in the latest data.

events.title: Kumanovo Agreement
events.summary: The Military Technical Agreement, also known as the Kumanovo Agreement, signed between the International Security Force (KFOR) and the Governments of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Serbia, was an accord concluded on 9 June 1999 in Kumanovo, Macedonia.

events.title: Twentieth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
events.summary: The Twentieth Amendment of the Constitution Act 2001 is an amendment to the Constitution of Ireland which provided constitutional recognition of local government and required that local government elections occur at least once in every five years. It was approved by referendum on 11 June 1999 and signed into law on 23 June of the same year.

events.title: 1999 Luxembourg general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Luxembourg on 13 June 1999, alongside European Parliament elections. The Christian Social People's Party remained the largest party, winning 19 of the 60 seats in the Chamber of Deputies. It formed a coalition government with the Democratic Party.

events.title: 1999 Melilla Assembly election
events.summary: The 1999 Melilla Assembly election was held on Sunday, 13 June 1999, to elect the 2nd Assembly of the Autonomous City of Melilla. All 25 seats in the Assembly were up for election.

events.title: Ante Jelavić takes power
events.summary: Ante Jelavić is a Bosnian Croat politician who served as the Croat member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1998 to 2001. He was the youngest person to hold the office of Presidency member and also the youngest Presidency member at the end of his tenure.

events.title: 1999 Latvian presidential election
events.summary: The 1999 presidential elections in Latvia took place on June 17, 1999. After no candidate collected the required number of votes in several ballots, a break was announced at the election session, during which Raimonds Pauls, who had received the most support at the time, withdrew his candidacy.

events.title: 25th G8 summit
events.summary: The 25th G8 Summit was held in Cologne, Germany, on 18–20 June 1999. The venue for this summit meeting was the Museum Ludwig in the central city.

events.title: Ehud Barak takes power
events.summary: Ehud Barak is an Israeli former general and politician who served as the prime minister of Israel from 1999 to 2001. He was leader of the Labor Party between 1997 and 2001 and between 2007 and 2011. He was also Minister of Defense from 2007 to 2013.

events.title: 1999 Iranian student protests
events.summary: The Iranian student protests of July 1999 were student protests which were violently repressed by the Basij and Ansar-e Hezbollah. Before the 2009 Iranian election protests, they were the most widespread and violent public protests to occur in Iran since the early years of the Iranian Revolution.

events.title: Guy Verhofstadt takes power
events.summary: Guy Maurice Marie Louise Verhofstadt is a Belgian politician who served as the prime minister of Belgium from 1999 to 2008. He was a member of the European Parliament (MEP) from Belgium from 2009 until 2024. Verhofstadt was a member of the Belgian Chamber of Representatives from 1985 to 2009.

events.title: Andris Šķēle takes power
events.summary: Andris Šķēle is a Latvian former politician and business oligarch. He served two terms as Prime Minister of Latvia from 1995 to 1997, and again from 1999 to 2000.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Djibouti vs FRUD-C
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Djibouti and FRUD-C over control of the government, starting 1999-07-24. This episode was active in 1 year (1999–1999), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1999-08-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Russia vs Chechen Republic of Ichkeria (Chechnya)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Russia (Soviet Union) and Chechen Republic of Ichkeria over control of Chechnya, starting 1999-08-11. This episode was active in 9 years (1999–2007), 4 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 2007-10-06.

events.title: Earthquake: 1999 İzmit earthquake
events.summary: An earthquake of moment magnitude 7.6 struck Kocaeli Province, Turkey, on 17 August 1999. According to official figures, at least 18,373 people died and 48,901 people were injured during the earthquake, and 5,840 people were missing. At least 155 deaths were associated with the tsunami.

events.title: Natural disaster: Hurricane Bret
events.summary: Hurricane Bret was the first of five Category 4 hurricanes that developed during the 1999 Atlantic hurricane season and the first tropical cyclone since Hurricane Jerry in 1989 to make landfall in Texas at hurricane intensity. Forming from a tropical wave on August 18, Bret slowly organized within weak steering currents in the Bay of Campeche.

events.title: 1999 East Timorese independence referendum
events.summary: An independence referendum was held in Indonesian-occupied East Timor on 30 August 1999, organised by United Nations Mission in East Timor. The referendum's origins lay with the request made by the President of Indonesia, B. J.

events.title: Mireya Moscoso takes power
events.summary: Mireya Elisa Moscoso Rodríguez is a Panamanian politician who served as the President of Panama from 1999 to 2004. She is the country's first and to date only female president.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Russia vs Wahhabi movement of the Buinaksk district (Dagestan)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Russia (Soviet Union) and Wahhabi movement of the Buinaksk district over control of Dagestan, starting 1999-09-02. This episode was active in 1 year (1999–1999), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1999-09-09.

events.title: Terrorist attack: 1999 Russian apartment bombings
events.summary: In September 1999, a series of explosions hit four apartment blocks in the Russian cities of Buynaksk, Moscow, and Volgodonsk, killing more than 300, injuring more than 1,000, and spreading a wave of fear across the country. The bombings, together with the 1999 war of Dagestan, triggered the Second Chechen War.

events.title: 1999 San Marino citizenship referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the citizenship law was held in San Marino on 12 September 1999. Voters were asked whether the new citizenship law passed on 16 June should come into force. Although a majority voted in favour, the quorum of 32% of registered voters (9,663) was not achieved and the referendum failed.

events.title: 1999 Algerian Civil Concord referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the Civil Concord Law was held in Algeria on 16 September 1999. The Civil Concord Law was an amnesty law that provided the legal framework to implement the 1995 "rahma" law promulgated by former President Liamine Zeroual. It was put forth by President Abdelaziz Bouteflika and adopted by parliament on 8 July 1999.

events.title: Franz Müntefering resigns as Federal Minister for Transport
events.summary: Franz Müntefering resigned as Federal Minister for Transport on 17 September 1999, having held the office since 27 October 1998.

events.title: 1999 Liberal Democratic Party presidential election
events.summary: The 1999 Liberal Democratic Party presidential election took place on 21 September 1999 to elect the leader and president of the Japanese Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).

events.title: Earthquake: 1999 Jiji earthquake
events.summary: The Chi-Chi earthquake, was a 7.3 ML or 7.7 Mw earthquake which occurred in Jiji (Chi-Chi), Nantou County, Taiwan on September 21, 1999, at 01:47:12 local time. 2,415 people were killed, 11,305 injured, and NT$300 billion worth of damage was done. It is the second-deadliest earthquake in Taiwan's recorded history, after the 1935 Shinchiku-Taichū earthquake.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs NLFT (Tripura)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and NLFT over control of Tripura, starting 1999-09-26. This episode was active in 6 years (1999–2004), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2004-12-28.

events.title: 1999 Tajik constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Tajikistan on 26 September 1999. The changes included legalising religious political parties, introducing a bicameral parliament, and lengthening the president's term from five to seven years. They were approved by 75% of voters, with a turnout of 93%.

events.title: 1999 Austrian legislative election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Austria on 3 October 1999. Although the Social Democratic Party remained the largest party in the National Council, a right-wing coalition government was formed by the Freedom Party of Austria (FPÖ) and the Austrian People's Party (ÖVP) after several months of negotiations.

events.title: 1999 Abkhazian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Abkhazia on 3 October 1999, alongside presidential elections. Voters were asked whether they approved of the constitution that had been approved by the Supreme Soviet on 26 November 1994, together with an amendment abolishing the life term for appointed judges and replacing it with five year terms.

events.title: Treaty signed: Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women
events.summary: The Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (OP-CEDAW) is an international treaty which establishes complaint and inquiry mechanisms for the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW).

events.title: 1999 Portuguese legislative election
events.summary: The 1999 Portuguese legislative election took place on 10 October. The election renewed all 230 members of the Assembly of the Republic.

events.title: Coup: 1999 Pakistani coup d'état
events.summary: The 1999 military takeover in Pakistan was a bloodless coup d'état initiated by the military staff at the Joint Staff HQ working under the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee and Chief of Army Staff General Pervez Musharraf.

events.title: European Council meeting (extraordinary)
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council (extraordinary meeting). Council presidency: Finland.

events.title: 1999 Swiss federal election
events.summary: Federal elections were held in Switzerland on 24 October 1999. Although the Swiss People's Party received the most votes for the first time in the party's history, the Social Democratic Party remained the largest party in the National Council, winning 51 of the 200 seats.

events.title: Assassination: Armenian parliament shooting
events.summary: The 1999 Armenian parliament shooting, commonly known in Armenia as October 27, was an attack on the Armenian National Assembly in the capital of Yerevan on 27 October 1999 by a group of five armed men led by Nairi Hunanyan that, among others, killed the two de facto decision-makers in the country's political leadership—Prime Minister Vazgen Sargsyan and…

events.title: Ilir Meta takes power
events.summary: Ilir Rexhep Meta is an Albanian politician who served as President of Albania from 2017 to 2022.

events.title: 1999 Georgian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Georgia on 31 October 1999, with second rounds in some constituencies on 7 and 14 November, and repeat elections in two constituencies on 28 November. The result was a victory for the Union of Citizens of Georgia, which won 131 of the 235 seats. Voter turnout was 67.9%

events.title: 1999 Ukrainian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Ukraine on 31 October 1999, with a second round on 14 November. The result was a victory for Leonid Kuchma, who defeated Petro Symonenko in the run-off, winning a second consecutive presidential election.

events.title: 1999 Uruguayan referendum
events.summary: A double referendum was held in Uruguay on 31 October 1999 alongside general elections. Voters were asked two questions; whether they approved of two initiatives, one on the financial autonomy of the judiciary, and one on preventing directors of state-owned companies from becoming MPs. Both were rejected by voters.

events.title: 1999 Australian republic referendum
events.summary: The Australian republic referendum held on 6 November 1999 was a two-question referendum to amend the Constitution of Australia. The first question asked whether Australia should become a republic, under a bi-partisan appointment model where the president would be appointed by the federal parliament with a two-thirds majority.

events.title: 1999 Guatemalan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Guatemala on 7 November 1999, with a second round of the presidential elections on 26 December. Alfonso Portillo won the presidential elections, whilst his Guatemalan Republican Front also won a majority of Congressional seats. Voter turnout was 53.8% on 7 November and 40.4% on 26 December.

events.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 1999
events.summary: The 1999 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting was the 16th Meeting of the Heads of Government of the Commonwealth of Nations. It was held in Durban, South Africa, between 12 November and 14 November 1999, and hosted by President Thabo Mbeki.

events.title: 1999 Latvian pensions referendum
events.summary: A referendum on state pensions was held in Latvia on 13 November 1999. A bill amending the state pension law had been passed by the Saeima on 5 August.

events.title: 1999 Macedonian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Macedonia on 31 October 1999, with a second round on 14 November. Tito Petkovski of the Social Democratic Union won the first round. However, as he received less than 50% of the vote, the election went to a second round, which was won by Boris Trajkovski of VMRO-DPMNE, who won 53.2% of the vote.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Iran vs MEK
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Iran and MEK over control of the government, starting 1999-11-25. This episode was active in 3 years (1999–2001), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 2001-09-16.

events.title: Vlatko Pavletić takes power
events.summary: Vlatko Pavletić was a Croatian politician, university professor, literary critic and essayist who served as acting President of Croatia from 1999 to 2000, as well as he served as Speaker of the Croatian Parliament from 1995 to 2000.

events.title: 1999 Seattle WTO protests
events.summary: The 1999 Seattle WTO protests, sometimes referred to as the Battle of Seattle, were a series of anti-globalization protests surrounding the WTO Ministerial Conference of 1999, where members of the World Trade Organization (WTO) convened at the Washington State Convention and Trade Center in Seattle, Washington on November 30, 1999.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Finland.

events.title: Alexandru Athanasiu takes power
events.summary: Alexandru Athanasiu is a Romanian politician and jurist. A former leader of the Romanian Social Democratic Party (PSDR), he has been a member of the Social Democratic Party (PSD) since 2001.

events.title: December 1999 Venezuelan constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Venezuela on 15 December 1999. Voters were asked whether they approved of the new constitution drawn up by the Constitutional Assembly elected earlier in the year. It was approved by 72% of voters, although turnout was only 44%.

events.title: 1999 Russian legislative election
events.summary: Legislative elections were held in Russia on 19 December 1999 to elect the 450 seats in the State Duma, the lower house of the Federal Assembly. Like in the previous elections in 1995, the electoral system resulted in many parties competing for the proportional seats and a significant number of independent deputies elected.

events.title: Mugur Isărescu takes power
events.summary: Constantin Mugur Isărescu is the governor of the National Bank of Romania, a position he has been holding since September 1990, with the sole exception of a period of time of one year, during which he served as Prime Minister of Romania. In addition, he is also a member of the Romanian Academy. Isărescu is a member of The Trilateral Commission.
